situation: When constructing our RGM events, we had some difficulty with creative designs, and communicating possible solutions for our individual events.
task_action: To overcome this problem, we first consulted with the rest of the team. In a team this should be the first step when you are presented with any problem. Referring to your team for help is useful for building greater teamwork, communication and problem solving skills. This method is not without its flaws, as creative solutions can be difficult to physically develop into a functional product. For certain problems it can also be very difficult to explain what the root cause of the problem is, even with the benefit of communication software like chatrooms and phone calls. Each team member is constructing and conducting tests individually in their own workspaces, and it can be very hard to offer solutions when each team member can't physically see the construction and determine the cause of the problem. After consolidating with the team, if the issue persists, it is also helpful to search resources online for similar problems or alternative methods for solutions.
result: The result from communicating solutions with team members is a stronger team. Sharing ideas with other people is a useful way to expand creative thinking skills, and develop more creative solutions to problems. The longer a team works together, they tend to develop similar ways of thinking and generating solutions, which helps in understanding the problem a team member is proposing. It then becomes easier to conceive a solution in a way that the team member will be able to understand and succeed upon. Online resources can help the team member find inspiration to potentially solve their problem or other collective issues the team may have. Online resources (e.g. videos) provide the ability to visualise a similar solution to your given problem. This will make it easier for the team member to solve their problem, developing their problem solving skills further.
pfr: When doing something for the first time, it can be difficult to make up solutions to new problems you haven't encountered before. It can be even harder to make any of these solutions work, which was a problem my team encountered. Through the duration of the assembly and testing process of the RGM development, we encountered problems with reliability and finding creative solutions to the project brief. When we communicated these issues to the rest of the team, ideas were proposed and tested accordingly. It was found through this testing that some solutions were unattainable with the material and environmental limitations of each team member. When this happened, we also made sure to check online resources for potential solutions as well. Due to the popularity of RGM's, we were successfully able to find some potential solutions that we could adapt to our own circumstances, however some solutions could not be found and had to be eliminated from the final project.
learning: If the solution could not be found after this effort, we deemed it acceptable to try a different method for the RGM so valuable time wasn't spent on an unattainable action for the final project. While it is always good to strive for excellence, sometimes approaching a difficult problem with unsuitable solutions is not the ideal way to complete a project brief with a given deadline. Even if this means sacrificing the very creative and elaborate actions planned in the brainstorming phase of project development, for more simple creative solutions to reach a finished product. In this way, our final project would be successfully completed by each team member, however the scale of creativity of our actions had to be lessened slightly in order to produce this successful product.

To ensure the completion of milestones by the deadline with maximum time and resource efficiency we employed time management strategies such as using the Priority Matrix software (based on the Eisenhower Method). The Gantt chart was chosen due to it's popularity as a project management tool, and as a tool to further simplify the Gantt chart, especially when there were multiple overlapping tasks. Ultimately, we found that clearly defining the project scope and mitigating risks, in addition to using good project managment tools improved our overall success as a group.

The experience of making the Gantt chart allowed us to appreciate the time and resource saving capabilities of simply having a comprehensive guide to key project milestones. situation: When approaching any engineering task, using data driven decision making is absolutely crucial. Collecting data in engineered structures allows engineers to have a clearer and scientifically supported understanding of their mechanism. By incorporating derived data into your decisions surrounding your product you will be able to produce a higher quality result. Through learning this during the ENGG1050 unit, the quality of our RGM machine was thus called into question when collecting data on the reliability of the machine to complete each individual function. We had many events in the function that originally had a low reliability score when tested 10 times. It was decided that we would need to have a discussion on how to improve these events and use our current data to assist our decisions.
task_action: Therefore, by utilising this method we held a team discussion on what areas of the questioned events was causing the weakness by analysing and assessing our current data. We next changed necessary variables in each event until the accuracy met the satisfaction of the entire team. This step was repeated a number of times to ensure the highest result was obtained, such as assessing whether a change in the weight of the ball, reinforcement of elements of the events or a multitude of things being incorporated simultaneously would produce the highest reliability score. When incorporating this tactic into our RGM machine my team and I were able to significantly improve our machine's accuracy and reliability, therefore increasing the overall quality of our product.
result: Through my team's shared desire to produce a high quality machine that could be reproducible due to high reliability scores we used our collection of data to effect our decisions of each individual event. This proved to be an incredibly efficient and effective tactic for our RGM. We are all very pleased with the new reliability results of our RGM with each event achieving at least 90% reliability.
pfr: The process of making critical data driven decisions as a group with a goal of achieving high reliability was trying and difficult at times, however, through working hard my team and I performed very well. I was thankful that my team and I were able to effectively communicate our ideas around what the data was reflecting, and what we could do to utilise this information in our decisions to each other in a professional capacity and practice patience, perseverance and flexibility. By remaining unbiased, we were able to listen to, critique and critically analyse data and discuss the effectiveness, weaknesses and ideas for improvement in reliability for each section. Our success in using data driven decision making is reflected through the smoothness of our filming stage which we were able to complete together in one group session.
learning: By approaching decision making in a methodical dat-driven approach my team and I were able to reach highly satisfying reliability and accuracy scores which filled us with confidence when entering our filming stage of the RGM. This is attributed to staying unbiased and openminded in the process, persevering until a decision wad been made in the same session so each idea was fresh in our minds and sharing a common goal of creating the most effective machine we were able to deliver in a timely manner. This experience of analysing data and thus making tough decisions around our overall event and function layout of our machine has demonstrated my teams positive and supportive group dynamic and reflects on our strong ability to work collaboratively. I feel that by using all of my engineering skills taught in this unit I was able to effectively analyse the data recorded to make beneficial decisions surrounding the future design of our RGM components with additional strength and understanding of how to effectively use data to aid design, thus developing a strong appreciation for the SPINE units that influenced my ability to achieve a strong final result in my group, particularly the 'Analysis' and 'Engineering Design' units.

topic: Trade-offs, judgment, and balance in resolution
situation: Throughout the second half of the semester, I have been unable to attend workshops as I had suddenly found employment during the break that required full-time attendance while training.
task_action: As my training for work now clashed with the time of the ENGG1050 workshop and my other classes, I had to make the right judgement on how to handle the situation and make trade-offs to achieve balance in my commitment to work and uni. As soon as I was aware of the fact that I had to attend my training full-time during when my classes would run, I had to make sure whether I could really commit to starting that job, as uni is my first priority. Initially, as was communicated to me, attending training meant I'd only have to miss the first two workshops and so I just let my team know of the situation and completed any work that needed to be done. I also stayed in contact with the team and talked to them regularly, especially before and after workshops to get caught up with everything. This way I could attend my work training while also not sabotaging my uni performance. As training finished, I learned that I'd have to do full-time consolidation for a few weeks as well. With the ENGG1050 workshop and my practicals that are hurdles, there was no way I could skip them all. So, after speaking with my manager I was able to obtain a few days off for my other mandatory practicals, and for the ENGG1050 workshop, as it wasn't a hurdle, I decided to continue with ensuring all the required work was being done, especially for the final RGM presentation.
result: By communicating effectively with my team and making the appropriate trade offs, I achieved a balance between work and uni. I can confidently say that our final RGM presentation is something our whole team can be proud of.
pfr: When I first got the new job offer, I was really proud of myself and excited to start, as the role was really good, had good pay and had room for growth in my career. However, I was feeling really anxious after learning that I'd need to attend full-time during training as I wanted to accept the role but uni was my first priority and if it jeopardised my studies, I'd have to reject the job offer. I was relieved, to find that training was only 4 weeks, so after the 2 weeks break, I'd only miss two workshops, which wasn't that bad. I was again stressing when I found out that consolidation was full-time too. My manager understood my situation and since I was meant to be a casual employee anyways, he gave me some leniency, but I thought it'd be best not to abuse it and only take days off for my mandatory uni classes, as I felt like not attending the workshops had zero impact on the final project as I was communicating with everyone regularly and I was watching all the lectures and doing the work, so I wasn't missing out on much from there either.
learning: I learned that good communication goes a long way. Even though I wasn't attending the workshops, simply being able to communicate my situation and working around that with the team, we overcame this little obstacle. I also learned how to make the right judgement in stressful situations to achieve balance. I obviously prioritised uni over work at this stage of my life, but being able to balance both out without too much strain on my studies is really great.

topic: Trade-offs, judgment, and balance in resolution
situation: One requirement of ENGG1050 is to hold weekly meetings to work on our RGM machine. This poses a challenge due to the varying schedules of our team members, where only a few members can consistently make it to the zoom meeting. The question arises of how we are going to make this work.
task_action: Keeping every team member up to date and on track with tasks ensures the ongoing development of our project. Consistency and communication is important not only to execute this project, but to do it to a high standard. With this in mind, we knew that we had to work with our unaligned schedules. Some questions that arise include how we would work with our unpredictable schedules. How would we make up for the missing members? Our solution includes using zoom, where a delegated chairperson would assign each person’s weekly work to be completed. Whatsapp would be used to relay this information, so that the remaining members are informed of their responsibilities for the week.
result: This is a trade-off of not having a set time for a live discussion, for our busy schedules. This is made up with the whatsapp group chat where no information is lost, only delayed. This ensures the balance of the work, and creates the expectation for everyone to complete the work despite meetings not being attended by everyone. The scheduling issue for each meting has been resolved and now everyone will be up to date thanks to utilising online resources.
pfr: One disadvantage of this system may be that clarification available in the zoom may not be available in the whatsapp, leading to an inaccuracy in the conveying of information and the feeling of being left out in the group. Also and not being able to have a live discussion as a team as a whole may hinder or delay the development of ideas and solutions thus being less efficient. This can lead to worries of aspects of our project not being acheived on time. However this trade off of efficiency for tending to other aspects of our lives works for our specific team where we are all satisfied with the distribution and communication of work. Us all being busy uni students has allowed this system to work as we can have empathy and respect for the fact that we all have our own lives, and one individuals schedule is bound to differ from the next’s.
learning: This situation can reflect other situations of our lives, where we have to balance work and life for our well being, in fact this may be seen across all other future units in our academic careers where putting energy into other aspects of our lives eg. health, social lives, may help us achieve higher grades in a way doing more work can't. There are always different combinations of trade offs that will work for each specific scenario and achieve the best outcomes for everyone and it is up to the individual to make that judgement.

situation: During the tense environment of my 12th-grade final exam, I was positioned next to a copycat girl. Initially, her subtle glances at my paper didn't bother me much, as I valued concentrating on my own task. After hours, her pestering grew annoying. She kept requesting me to repeat my answers quietly. To protect my academic integrity, I cautioned her to fear the examiner's keen eye because expulsion was guaranteed if he saw us. Though severe, my words didn't discourage her. Then suddenly she boldly slid my paper across the desk into the dangerous no-man's land between us. My heart raced between right and obsessive craving for an easy way out as I watched my hard-earned work teeter towards deceit. My nerve-wracking choice determined my fate and character.
task_action: My tolerance for the girl's flagrant plagiarism on my paper was becoming thin. I asked her calmly but firmly to stop because her behaviour was unfair to me and violated the standards of honesty and academic integrity that should be upheld during tests. With every word, I made an effort to emphasise the importance of honesty, and our academic career should be a reflection of our genuine abilities, not a mere facade based on dishonesty. I spoke about the moral obligation we had to uphold to both the responsibilities we carried as students and the moral duty we owed to ourselves and our education. She kept trying to ignore me, but I was adamant that I would uphold these principles. I came to the realisation that our behaviour in the test room would define who we are as people more so than the grade we obtained. This was more than just an intellectual test; it was also a moral character test. And I was determined to do it while upholding my moral principles.
result: My pulse raced as the teacher's attention focused on our desk. Surprisingly audaciously, the girl seated next to me charged that I had taken her paper and placed it in the center. I was called out in front of the entire class as being a dishonest student. The most painful part of my friends' shock was watching them try to share this bogus story with the friend they knew. The humiliation pierced faith with a profound, knife-like wound. However, I refused to back down and said the truth. The trick was eventually exposed by the teacher, and justice was done. Although the humiliation hurt, it strengthened my resolve to be honest and ethical, and my friends gradually came to realise the reality. And that girl had been expelled for the final exam.

In those tense moments, I watched as the cloud of suspicion hung over me, casting doubt on my integrity. After proving myself innocent, and as the real story unfolded, the weight of embarrassment lifted, and understanding washed over the faces of my classmates. They realized that I had been a victim of deceit, not a perpetrator of dishonesty. This experience left an indelible mark on me. It reinforced my belief in the importance of ethics and honesty in every aspect of life. It served as a reminder that social responsibility is not just a concept but a vital practice. In that classroom, I learned that we should all be steadfast in our commitment to honesty, integrity, and responsibility, for they are the pillars that uphold a just and honorable society. This is obvious that our integrity is part of our social responsibility because many people will suffer as a result of our actions.
learning: This exam coping event in my life taught me a valuable lesson, instilling in me the indisputable value of ethics, honesty, and societal duty. It was a turning point in my life that inspired a lifelong dedication to these ideals and a strong desire to inspire others to embrace them as well. I determined that day that I would never, ever compromise my own honesty, even in the face of tragedy. Being genuine to oneself, I realised, is a beacon of light that can guide us through life's harshest storms.But the lesson went beyond my actions. I realised it was my responsibility to champion these ideas in the world around me. I became an advocate for integrity, attempting to set a good example and inspire everyone around me to follow suit. This incident became a pillar of my values, a story I would tell others to emphasise the pervasiveness of ethics, honesty, and social duty. topic: The impact of engineering on society and the environment
situation: Engineering has had a profound and far-reaching impact on both society and the environment. It has played a vital role in shaping the modern world, contributing to both progress and challenges. Here, we will explore the various impacts that engineering has had on society and the environment.
task_action: The actions taken by engineers or overall, the impact of engineering on society and the environment, has been clearly shown, as engineers themselves design, construct and maintain the systems, buildings and technologies that enhance societies quality of life. Infrastructure development, healthcare advancements, energy generation and efficiency, are among a few of the impacts engineering has had on society. Engineering’s influence on the environment exhibits a diverse range of impacts, covering both favorable and the adverse aspects. Detrimental outcomes of engineering on the environment include pollution, deforestation, and the generation of waste, among other adverse effects. As well as, engineering also yields beneficial impacts, such as the promotion of renewable energy, the development of sustainable infrastructure, and improvements in energy efficiency, are among many positive contributions. In order to improve connection and facilitate the efficient movement of people and products, infrastructure development engineers have constructed essential infrastructures including roads, bridges, and transportation systems. Medical device, diagnostic, treatment, and outcome improvements have all improved thanks to engineering innovations in healthcare. Engineers have created and improved energy sources like solar, wind, and hydraulic power sources, which have led to the clean and more effective production of energy. THE NEGATIVE IMPACTS ENGINEERING HAS HAD ON THE ENVIRONMENT: Industrial operations, transportation, and energy production have had a significant negative impact on the environment, contaminating the air and water supplies, endangering human health, and degrading ecosystems. Some engineering projects call for the development of industrial and urban areas, which has resulted in habitat degradation and deforestation, endangering biodiversity. The majority of engineering projects have all led to the production of solid and hazardous waste, both of which are harmful to human health and ecosystems. THE POSITIVE IMPACTS ENGINEERING HAS HAD ON THE ENVIRONMENT: Having developed and promoted alternative energy sources like solar, wind, and hydropower, we as a society are using fewer fossil fuels and emitting fewer greenhouse gas emissions. Engineering has also resulted in significant advancements in the energy efficiency of industries, transportation, and infrastructure, lowering energy consumption and having a less negative impact on the environment. Engineers are always coming up with new and better ways to build a building with sustainability in mind, including green building techniques, efficient transportation methods, and eco-friendly building materials.
result: The effects of engineering on society and the environment are quite varies. Through technical advancements, economic expansion, and healthcare innovations, it has improved society’s quality of life. Although, it has also brought forth problems for the environment, such as pollution, climate change, and resource depletion. Engineers are putting more emphasis on sustainable solutions to lessen these negative impacts and creating a more balanced future for society as well as the environment.
pfr: When I first learned about how engineering has impacted society and the environment, I had a lot of thoughts about both positive and negative, about how engineering has impacted the world. On one hand, I feel a sense of pride in the remarkable achievements of engineers in improving the quality of life for countless of people. Engineering had brought us, conveniences (roads, transport, and many more), increased access to information, and improved healthcare, which has positively impacted the way of living for society. Although, I also experience a sense of guilt, there is a growing awareness of the negative consequences of engineering on the environment. The production and disposal or electronic waste, depletion of natural resources, and the contribution to climate change are some of the environmental consequences that engineering has inadvertently worsened.
learning: To address these challenges, engineers must adopt a comprehensive and ethical mindset to handle these challenges. Sustainable techniques are crucial, including developing eco-friendly products and infrastructure, cutting waste, and utilizing renewable energy sources. Finding creative ways to reduce the harmful effects of engineering also requires encouraging collaboration between engineers, legislators, and environmental experts. Engineers should also constantly educate themselves on the latest developments in environmentally friendly technologies and promote ethical practices withing businesses and industries. By integrating sustainability principles into engineering education and professional development, we can ensure that future engineers prioritize environmental consciousness in their work.

situation: 2 people from our group withdrew from the unit, leaving the group with only 3 members.
task_action: We needed to decide which elements of the project were the most important to complete, knowing that some aspects would need to be sacrificed as we did not have enough people to complete the entire project. We organised a group meeting outside of class time to delegate the most important tasks amongst ourselves. We also discussed which aspects of the project were the least important, and hence which tasks would only be worked on if the most important parts were completed with time to spare.
result: We each made a commitment to dedicate time to complete our sections in order not to let the rest of the group down, and get the best mark possible. We decided that finer details in the model such as stairs, rooftop spaces and landscaping would not be prioritised until the majority of the model and report were completed to a high standard.
pfr: It was quite daunting knowing that our group had 2 less members than every other group and I was not sure that we would be able to complete everything to a high standard. This made me feel very overwhelmed as I am a high achieving student and am not comfortable with submitting work that does not meet requirements and expectations. As a result of this, I overloaded myself with work to try and make up for the absence of other people in the group and this made me feel quite stressed.
learning: Through this process I have learned how important delegation is, as well as knowing your own limits. After allocating various parts of the project to the two other members in the group, the task felt much more achievable as it no longer felt like the entire assignment was resting on my shoulders. It also taught me that sometimes you can't do everything, and that it's important to prioritise your own wellbeing, rather than attempting to complete something that is designed for 5 people (not for 3).

Recognizing the urgency of the situation at hand, I embraced taking immediate action as crucial for making informed decisions about my future endeavors. I also remained openminded to new opportunities and ideas while exploring additional hobbies such as playing the violin that would contribute to my personal growth. Notably, watching the Formula 1 has solidified my passion for this career path and further empowered me to adjust and thrive in ever-changing circumstances when required.
result: Through my journey of self-discovery and personal growth I embarked on a transformative path by transferring to an engineering program. The task was to come up with a creative and visually appealing sequence of events that would captivate our audience and execute the intended tasks. We began by clearly articulating the problem statement, which was to design a series of interconnected steps that would ultimately lead to a chain reaction, accomplishing a specific final goal. During the session, establish teamwork by encouraging everyone to share their ideas freely, no matter how unconventional. We used the gallery method of brainstorming, where each idea was written on a sticky note and posted on a Miro wall for all to see. This allowed us to build upon each other's concepts.
result: After finalizing the concept, we recognized the importance of breaking down the tasks further. We divided the sequence into individual components, each assigned to a specific team member based on their strengths and expertise. The collaborative brainstorming session resulted in a well-defined and creative sequence of events for our Rube Goldberg Machine project.

The prospect of creating a chain reaction for the machine was exciting, but I was unsure if our team could effectively collaborate and come up with a cohesive design. However, there were moments when disagreements arose from split opinions about the design, but we were able to overcome this as a group through communication by listening to both opinions and collectively as a group voted for which idea we thought was more appropriate for our final design.
learning: The insight I gained from this experience is the important role of open communication and collaboration in problem-solving. It reinforced the idea that no answers are perfect the first time and that diverse viewpoints can help to consolidate the foundation of the initial design, leading to better solutions. In the future, I will approach teamwork and brainstorming sessions with a greater appreciation for the value of each team member's input. I will actively work toward creating an environment where everyone feels comfortable sharing their ideas, even if they differ from the majority. Additionally, I've learned to be more patient and open to alternative viewpoints, recognizing that they can lead to more innovative and well-rounded solutions.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: The situation for the chosen topic is the two weeks before my HSC (High School Certificate) final Year 12 exams in 2022, which would determine my final grade and the degree I would be eligible for. I had my 18th birthday and my Year 12 formal party during this two-week period, making it incredibly challenging to manage studying and having fun. I was unable to enjoy these 2 major events that one only gets to experience once because of the stress of the final exams, which had now begun to set in. As a result, even though I wanted to completely enjoy my 18th birthday party and my Year 12 formal, I couldn't help but feel a constant sense of urgency as I thought about the final exams, which were constantly lingering at the back of my mind. Hence, I had to find a way to manage my time, have the will to deliver and become flexible such that I didn’t regret not enjoying these events but also not regretting that I didn’t study enough for the exams.
task_action: To ensure that I enjoyed my time during these 2 once in a lifetime events and also did my best in the HSC, I had to implement certain time and resource management strategies. These tactics made sure I always had the perseverance and drive to succeed. I was able to maximise my productivity while studying using these techniques, which allowed me to have a greater amount of time to enjoy my 18th birthday party and my formal. The very first step I took was to plan ahead, as time itself is also a very important resource. I utilised Google Calendar to break each day up into study sections. Each section was 1-2 hours, depending on how much work needed to be done. Each section would only focus on one subject at a time. During these study sections I would either go through my flashcards using an app called Anki (which utilises the study method called spaced repetition) or I would attempt practice exams and reattempt the ones that I got wrong. By reattempting questions I got wrong I was able to gain maximum benefits out of the practice papers which were limited. Moreover, Anki would give me daily notifications to remind me that I had a certain amount of flashcards to finish before the end of the day. This ensured that I was able to deliver and not become too overwhelmed by the sense of urgency. The next action I took was setting clear priorities. As the dates of each exam was spread out, I would spend more time on the subject that had its test the earliest. Next, I would prioritise topics within each subject whereby I knew I had gaps in my knowledge. This enabled me to not only reinforce what I knew but also ensure that I wasn’t going into my exams without knowing everything that I needed to. By doing so, I was able to use the limited time resources I had and ensure I was doing the best I could. As I knew I was doing the best I could, I had moments where I felt calm and the lingering stress was decreased. This motivated me to persevere through the following weeks without drowning in an ocean of anxiety and self-doubt. Another step that I took was to focus on one task at a time. Rather than thinking about each subject as a whole, I made a To Do list on Google Keep which enabled me to break the subject down into parts. This reduced the stress greatly as larger topics were broken down into more mentally digestible smaller topics. This also increased how flexible I could be when creating my study timetable.
result: The aim of my actions were to maximise the use of the little time I had to study for my exams so that I would be able to enjoy my 18th birthday party and my Year 12 formal party. The result of my actions was that I was able to fully enjoy the two events with only almost no negative effects on my exams. I had attempted each test to the best of my ability and I was confident that I was going to receive the mark that I wanted. I had not regretted enjoying the parties or wishing that I spent more time studying for my exams. Moreover I had very little stress during the exams. When I got my ATAR (final mark) back, I had accomplished the initial goal that I had set. However I was certain that I could’ve done better by not attending the parties, but this didn’t bother me as I knew it would’ve had no extra benefit as I achieved the goal I wanted to. In the end, I had no regrets and I achieved the initial task that I had set out to complete.
pfr: Before I set out to efficiently study by utilising the aforementioned techniques, I was quite overwhelmed with the workload and very stressed. This affected other areas of my life such as not getting enough exercise or eating properly. I held the thought that I was going to fail my exams and I would not get into the degree I wanted. I thought that my future would be ruined and on top of all of that I would not be able to enjoy my 18th birthday party or my formal party. However after implementing the strategies I was more confident than I had ever been about any exam I ever took. As these strategies enabled me to become more resourceful and flexible, while studying I had developed a sense of perseverance that didn’t falter once. This ensured that the lingering sense of stress and urgency I had, would be kept at bay and wouldn’t overwhelm me. During the exams, I didn’t pay much attention to whether or not I had enjoyed my parties and my only focus was doing the best I could in the exam. However, after the exams I was content and joyful with what I had done, as I had not only done above what I expected in my exams but also enjoyed my parties.
learning: By using the study techniques I was able to achieve all the goals I had set out before the exams. I learnt that it was futile for me to be stressed before the exams because I should have been confident when I implemented the strategies. I learnt how to persevere through any task, regardless of how daunting it may seem initially. Moreover, I learnt how to fully maximise my time and organise tasks efficiently and the importance of being resourceful and flexible. I have been able to carry forward these skills into university and I have constantly been on top of my lectures, quizzes and assignments with minimal stress. Through this experience I have learnt not only these vital time and resource management skills but also how to reduce stress and have a more positive mindset when faced with larger workloads.

situation: As part of our engineering class project, we designed a Rube Goldberg machine to showcase the principles of physics and engineering in a fun and engaging manner. task_action: I took on the responsibility of delivering an oral presentation for a number of weeks explaining the mechanics and purpose of our machine whilst showcasing our preparation work. To do this effectively, we first broke down the machine's operation into its individual components and steps. I worked with my team to gather visuals, slow-motion videos, and step-by-step explanations of each part. Then, our group crafted a narrative around the machine’s operation that was both engaging and educational. By using anecdotes, humor such as memes and images, and relatable comparisons, I aimed to make the complexities of the machine accessible to everyone.
result: The audience was deeply engaged during the presentation's. The visuals and step-by-step breakdown made it easy for them to follow the flow of the machine. The feedback was overwhelmingly positive, with many stating they had a clear understanding of how our Rube Goldberg machine worked and the science behind it. The teacher commended our team not only on the machine's design but also on our ability to communicate its intricacies effectively.
pfr: When faced with the challenge of presenting our Rube Goldberg machine, a whirlwind of emotions enveloped me. I felt pride in our creative endeavor, but an undercurrent of apprehension tugged at me, given the machine's intricate design. I wondered if I could effectively break down its complexities to resonate with our audience. CONNECTIONS TO PAST EXPERIENCES: Previous presentations I'd been part of echoed in my memory, reminding me that successful communication is not just about content but delivery. There were moments in the past when I hadn't tailored my approach to the audience, leading to less impactful presentations. Drawing from those lessons, I anchored this presentation with engaging visuals and analogies that could bridge any gaps in understanding.
learning: The experience solidified a vital understanding for me while knowledge and content are foundational, the way they areconveyed can make or break the audience's engagement. situation: Over the past 6 years I have worked professionally as a Diagnostic Radiographer across many public and private healthcare facilities. To this day I can still recollect my very first nightshift, and the experiences that I had learnt from it. Working in the Townsville University Hospital this night, I was the sole radiographer providing all the Medical Imagining services across both Xray and CT for the entire hospital. It was a busy night and at some point, I received two phone calls within seconds of each other, one was theatre stating they had an anesthetised patient on the table and needed x-rays, and the other was a MET (Medical emergency team) Call attending a patient with acute shortness of breath that needed me also. As I was leaving the workstation to change into my theatre attire, there was an announcement made through the emergency PA system “Paediatric Rapid Response to RESUS”.
task_action: I immediately called the second on-call Radiographer, explained what was happening and asked them come in. I got changed into scrubs, informed ED and the MET call team that I had to attend theatre urgently and that another radiographer would be there shortly. Once I had finished screening (taking x-rays) for the theatre case, I returned to the medical imaging department, sent the on-call radiographer home and continued the rest of the shift. Although I applied good critical thinking to able to overcome this sudden spike in the workload, I wanted to make a change, so that something like this would not happen again, to myself or my colleagues. So, I approached my team leader with my concerns about the increased workload and the pressure it has on the sole nightshift radiographer, especially the less experienced graduates (as I was). I also addressed the issue, with statistics I had gathered, in staff meetings and with the deputy director at the time advocating for increased support for the nightshift radiographer and especially for graduates undertaking nightshift for the first time.
result: At the Townsville University Hospital, I have since been the last radiographer to ever (since 2019) work their first nightshift alone. As part of my advocating for a change and the support of my colleagues, the first initial nightshift for any new staff member is rostered with a ‘buddy’, another experienced radiographer to help guide them through the afterhours procedures and processes. Although I did also advocate for a second radiographer to be rostered to nightshift indefinitely due to the increased workload, I cannot claim that I was reason that they decided to do so. COVID-19 and the increased workload that came with it was, but I supported this and undertook additional nightshifts to help the nightshift radiographer.
pfr: The nightshift in which this whole sequence of events happened was one of the worst, if not the worst shift, I have worked in my entire professional career. I was a graduate radiographer, extremely stressed due to the unusually busy night and with added emergency calls, I just couldn’t keep on top of everything and called for help, twice. Before the theatre call even took place, I had called the first on-call, the CT radiographer and asked if they could come in to help, but I was told, “Stop stressing, I’m not coming in, it’s your first night. You’ll be fine”. This did not make me stop stressing, but made me feel even worse, like I had no support at all. I was extremely thankful for the support that the second on-call radiographer provided when I called them, they calmly advised me on what I should do and handled the whole situation professionally. However, I was angered by initial lack of support and how we as graduate radiographers are put into situations like this in the first place, I wanted it to change. With a newfound determination I retrospectively produced stats showcasing the increasing workload endured by the nightshift radiographer from the past few years and created surveys which I distributed to my fellow colleagues in order to prove to management that something needed to change.
learning: Through this experience, I gained several valuable insights that have shaped my approach towards work and advocacy. The lack of support I initially encountered underscored the vital role of teamwork and mentorship, especially for less experienced staff. It taught me the significance of fostering a supportive work environment where colleagues can rely on each other during high-pressure situations. Confronted with the overwhelming workload and inadequate support systems in place, I realized the necessity of proactive advocacy for institutional change. By gathering data and engaging with management, I proved the need for additional resources and support for nightshift radiographers. This experience taught me the power of advocacy in effecting positive change within the workplace.

situation: In order to complete this task and all of its extensions, I had to use critical thinking and problem-solving skills in order to construct a dynamic algorithm that could facilitate a seemingly infinite amount of gestures. In short, how could I use maths to find the relationship between numbered gestures, no matter the amount of gestures?

From observing the lines drawn to indicate which gestures would win and lose against others, I noticed that each gesture loses to half of the gestures that are immediately clockwise from itself and wins against the remaining half of the gestures that are counter-clockwise from itself. With that in mind, I began trying to express this relationship using maths. After a few attempts at nailing the formula, I began implementing the algorithm in code.

CODE REVIEW AND DEBUGGING: I meticulously reviewed the Arduino code responsible for interfacing with the simulated sensors within the Tinkercad environment. I debugged the code to identify any logical errors, syntax issues, or inaccuracies in the data processing algorithms. VIRTUAL TESTING SCENARIOS: To diagnose the sensor inaccuracies, I created a series of virtual testing scenarios within the Tinkercad simulation environment. These scenarios simulated various real-world conditions and sensor inputs to evaluate the system's response and identify potential sources of error. DATA VISUALIZATION: Utilizing Tinkercad's data visualization tools, I monitored and analyzed the sensor readings in real-time during the virtual testing scenarios. This allowed me to visualize the data trends, anomalies, and inconsistencies, facilitating the identification of underlying issues. PARAMETER ADJUSTMENT: Based on the analysis of simulated sensor data, I adjusted the simulation parameters such as sensor calibration values, noise levels, and environmental factors to better reflect real-world conditions and improve the accuracy of the sensor readings. SIMULATION REFINEMENT: Through an iterative process of testing, analysis, and refinement, I fine-tuned the Tinkercad simulation settings and code implementations to mitigate sensor inaccuracies and enhance the reliability of the smart home automation system simulation.
result: * ENHANCED SIMULATION ACCURACY: By identifying and addressing the underlying causes of sensor inaccuracies within the Tinkercad simulation environment, I successfully improved the accuracy of the simulated sensor readings. * INCREASED RELIABILITY: The implemented solutions ensured consistent and reliable sensor data within the Tinkercad simulation, enabling the smart home automation system to function reliably and accurately in virtual scenarios. * PROJECT ADVANCEMENT: With the sensor accuracy issue resolved, the project progressed smoothly, meeting its objectives of simulating a functional smart home automation system within the Tinkercad environment.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: I have been working on a (fairly ambitious) software project since year 7. This project repeatedly outgrew my programming and project management skills and became unmaintainable.
task_action: Identifying what was wrong with the previous version of the software and thinking about how I should move forward. In the beginning, I couldn't program, so I learnt. I did a lot of prototyping to gain concrete experience with programming languages, libraries and techniques. I then structured my next iteration differently, applying my new knowledge and skills.

learning: Although I have ultimately persevered with this project, I have learnt that giving up entirely and restarting is a big effort and setback, and should only be reserved for the biggest of messes. I have recently been refactoring my software and cleaning up what I have, rather than starting again. This has led to more progress and more success. I have been learning discipline, especially throughout the HSC and now in my first semester of university. Equipped with this, I am better tackling the hard and boring problems despite the will to just move on to something more interesting. The ability to persevere, even when it needs discipline, is a valuable skill that I hope to continue developing throughout my whole life.

learning: From this reflection, I've learned the crucial role that structured critique plays in the brainstorming process. Maintaining an environment where team members feel valued and heard is essential for fostering innovation. Reflecting on this experience has reinforced my understanding of the multidimensional roles and responsibilities of engineers, which extend beyond technical tasks to include leadership, teamwork, and strategic decision-making. situation: I was required to draw 3 different diagrams of a 3D-printed object, in order to communicate the size and properties of the object on paper.
task_action: First the object was drawn in 2 point perspective, utilising two vanishing points two effectively convey the 3 dimensional nature of the object and a separate, detachable piece in two separate drawings. This 3D nature was further expanded on in my isometric drawing, where the x and z axes of the object were each drawn 30 degrees from the horizontal. Finally, I drew a multi-view drawing of the 3D-printed object, using 2D perspectives from it's top, front and side views to portray it's shape from different angles in a detailed manner. In order to ensure the readers understanding of the object, a detachable piece of the object was drawn separately, using appropriate labelling to communicate it's cylindrical nature. The drawing was made in a 3:1 scale and included appropriately labelled dimensioning to accurately convey the size of the object.
result: 5 drawings were made, each with their appropriate features in order to communicate the shape, size and nature of the provided object.
pfr: The multi-view drawing was approached methodically and accurately. With the correct use of a compass and the provided tools I was able to provide two neat, accurate and informative portrayals of the 3D-printed object and the detached piece from all 3 perspectives. The isometric drawing was informative, well scaled, using accurately measured 30 degree angles and sizing to convey the 3 dimensional features of the object. This drawing, however was not as neat as it could have been and only consisted of the main piece of the object, primarily because of the circular holes, which were drawn in freehand in the interest of time. The 2 point perspective, on the other hand, included both drawings, with the sketch of the main piece, providing accurate placement of vanishing points and their respective lines. This main piece, however, was too small to utilise the space on the A3 paper well, due to the 1:1 scale, while the detached piece was done in correct scale. The detached piece was not as neat and did not effectively utilise the vanishing points as there was not enough time to consider the neatness and orientation of the piece.
learning: Overall time management could have been utilised better, as too much time was spent perfecting the multi-view drawing, leaving little time to consider neatness and plan for the isometric and 2 point perspective drawings. Additionally, I learned the compass should have been better utilised in these two drawings, as I did not employ the correct method of drawing circles at angles, often leaving them messy and inaccurate.

situation: I am a cultural dance instructor and during the COVID-19 lockdown, I faced the challenge of transitioning my teaching and choreography sessions to online. task_action: Despite the limitations of remote learning, my primary task was to ensure that I could maintain the quality of teaching and choreography for my students. Additionally, we had to prepare them for an upcoming competition that was scheduled shortly after the lockdown ended. This meant not only maintaining their skills but also ensuring that they were competition-ready despite the unconventional circumstances. ACTION: I adopted several strategies to approach and tackle this challenge. Firstly, I focused on developing my patience and communication skills, realising that teaching over video calls requires clearer and more detailed explanations. I also dedicated extra time to individual feedback and support to compensate for the lack of in-person interaction. As the competition drew nearer, I intensified and became stricter on punctuality and performance, ensuring that despite the limitations of remote learning, my students were on track and competition-ready. I provided personalised feedback and guidance to each dancer, focusing on areas of improvement and refining our routines to perfection.
result: Despite the initial challenges and the abrupt transition to online teaching, all of our efforts paid off. When the lockdown ended and the competition took place, my students showcased a remarkable performance. Out of five competing teams, we secured second place, a testament to the hard work and resilience of both myself and my students. The transition into remote teaching not only allowed us to adapt to unforeseen circumstances but also enabled us to emerge stronger and more capable as a team, showing greater potential within them. We successfully navigated the challenges posed by the pandemic and proved that with determination and adaptability, we could overcome any obstacle.
pfr: Reflecting on the experience of transitioning to online teaching and preparing my students for a competition during the lockdown evokes a mix of emotions. Initially, I felt overwhelmed and apprehensive about how effectively I could adapt to remote teaching and maintain the standard of instruction I strive for. Throughout the experience, I experienced moments of frustration and doubt, especially when faced with technical glitches or communication barriers during online sessions. There were times when I questioned whether I was providing enough support and guidance to my students, given the limitations of remote teaching. However, seeing their dedication and progress served as a constant source of motivation and reassurance.
learning: This experience has provided invaluable insights into the importance of adaptability, resilience, and effective communication in navigating challenging circumstances. I've learned that flexibility is key to overcoming unexpected obstacles and that embracing change with an open mind can lead to growth and innovation. The goal was to ensure the algorithm could reliably determine the winner in a game with up to 11 different gestures. I developed a mathematical model where each gesture was assigned a unique value, and the winner could be determined through simple arithmetic operations based on these values. I then coded the new algorithm, integrated it into the existing game framework, and conducted multiple rounds of testing to ensure its accuracy and efficiency.
result: The implementation of the modular arithmetic-based algorithm was a success. It not only reduced the complexity of the game logic significantly but also improved the execution speed. The new algorithm could effortlessly determine the winner among the 11 gestures, maintaining game fairness and enhancing user experience. This approach also enhanced the game's maintainability, making it easier to add more gestures in the future if needed.

The initial algorithm, while adequate for fewer gestures, became cumbersome and less efficient as more gestures were added. This challenge put my problem-solving skills to the test, and admittedly, I was unsure whether I could devise a solution that maintained both the integrity and performance of the game. However, as I delved deeper into potential solutions, my anxiety transformed into excitement. The process of researching, designing, and testing the new algorithm became a journey of discovery, revealing new ways to apply mathematical concepts to real-world applications.

First, it underscored the importance of adopting a flexible and open-minded approach when tackling complex problems. The modular arithmetic solution emerged only after I considered several potential strategies, which highlighted the necessity of thorough exploration before settling on a solution. Second, I learned that simplicity often trumps complexity in design. The elegance of the modular arithmetic approach not only solved the problem but did so in a way that was more maintainable and scalable than the original method. This insight has led me to appreciate the power of mathematical simplicity and its application in software development. Finally, the experience has profoundly impacted how I will approach future engineering challenges. I've learned the value of stepping back to assess the bigger picture—especially in situations where initial solutions don't adequately solve the problem. Moving forward, I will incorporate a phase of broad research and conceptual experimentation before honing in on a specific solution. This broader initial approach will help ensure that I am not only solving problems more effectively but also innovating in ways that could lead to better overall outcomes. This project has instilled a greater confidence in me to handle uncertainty and complexity in my future engineering career. It has also highlighted the importance of critical thinking and the role it plays in the innovation process, reinforcing that every problem, no matter how daunting initially, can be approached systematically and effectively solved with the right strategies and mindset.

situation: During my first semester of university, which involved a combination of in-person lectures and tutorials, online learning, and attending in-person practicals when needed. At first it was kind of intimidating, all the new people, the new tutors and lecturers and the way that everything was done was completely different to high school. However, I knew that if I wanted my studies to thrive then I needed to learn effective communication. Communication between fellow students to stay in the loop of everything and tutors and lectures to make sure I understand everything being taught and shown to me.

result: And it worked: I gained a greater understanding, formed relationships, had more confidence and was more successful in my studies. I learned that effective academic communication requires being actively engaged, giving, and receiving timely feedback, and respecting boundaries.

I’ve been giddy with confidence when my arguments made sense, angry when jargon muddied my messages, and proud when I came up with a persuasive pitch. Those emotions are my needle: with them, I keep myself honest. I’ve come to see that good communication has nothing to do with pretty rhetoric; it’s all about connection. It’s about taking something with layers and making it translucent, like attaching a circuit to a circuit board.
learning: My big takeaway? Simple rules are good ones: simple language resonates when drafting an email, or in presenting a project; simple listening connects me more deeply to others; simple improvisation transforms my stories and helps me adapt creatively to different industries and cultures. When I blend all these ideas, empathy will be a core asset of my strategy. I'll be crisp and compassionate with my words; grow my narratives through listening; lean into the discomfort that signals I'm learning; and rely on my team for direction when I'm feeling lost. This journey is the experience of every engineer - a symphony of building, bumbling, testing, tweaking and growing.

situation: My first workshop was the engineering machining workshop. I had to learn engineering practices by building an aluminium toolbox for which I was given instructions on how to do so. This tested areas related to my chosen topic on 'the impact of engineering on society and the environment', including, material management (impact on the environment) and quality of the build (impact on society).
task_action: I individually built my toolbox and thus had the responsibility to manage time and materials. Although I had to be relatively quick to finish the project, I simultaneously had to take my time in order to not waste my materials. In addition I had to make sure that the project was of a high quality finish so that it could function the way it was intended and function well. Action: In order to not have a negative impact on the environment, I had to make sure that I used my materials wisely. Firstly within the room, the students all cut up large pieces of metal in order to not waste what was there. However individually, I always made sure that I measured multiple times before cutting. This allowed me to understand exactly what I was to be left with, know that it would look correct, and know where to cut. This was important because I wanted to minimise my waste material by cutting off as little as possible, and make sure I would not have to use more material if I had to start over due to the cut being wrong. In addition, the workshop minimised the impact on the environment by reusing wood as a base plate, having a scrap metal bin where metal could be reused and used a more wise material - that being metal and not plastic and so I participated in these workshop practices. In order to have a good impact on society through engineering, I took my time with the project, making sure not to rush anything, to have a good quality product by the end of the workshop. This allowed me to have a high quality product in which it could last a long time and function just as it was intended. By doing this, the project can positively impact the society by having a durable, lasting, good product to use that can be trusted. This is especially true for workers as it can make their job easier by not only having the product in the first place but by also having it of a good quality and satisfies them. By having this product of a high quality, it sets me up to continue on this path of quality throughout my engineering journey and thus this will positively impact society by having a decent engineer work for the better of society. Having a product that does not negatively impact the environment also in turn positively impacts society as the product made will make society live in a better environment but it also lets them live in peace of mind knowing the product they are using was made with the environment in mind - attempting to help heal it.
result: By putting these actions together throughout the workshop time, I was able to confidently learn engineering practices and make my aluminium toolbox while attempting to make it have a better impact on the environment rather than using way too much material and wasting lots of material. In turn by doing this I positively impacted society by not damaging the environment further and also gifting this to another member of society so they can use it and make their work easier, to which, brought them satisfaction.
pfr: This workshop experience initially seemed very environmentally damaging due to the amount of students and amount of materials that needed to be used. However, after realising how to simply focus on what I can do for my own project environmentally, it helped to realise that I can only do what I can do to make my project as environmentally friendly as possible and still be able to learn engineering practices. In addition, by making a product I am proud of, of a high quality not only shows me what I can achieve but means that I can share it with society to improve on it and improve satisfaction. The toolbox that I made is also a product that has functionality after finishing the workshop and after learning the skills required for engineering and thus is not wasteful due to the use after and the important practical skills learnt throughout the workshop.
learning: I learned through this experience that I just need to focus on what I can do within a project. In addition I learnt that small changes to a project can add up, for example all the small steps I took to ensure my impact on the environment could be low, all added up. Thus, I learnt that I can do the same for all my future engineering projects and make sure that I always keep the environment in my mind when completing projects. In addition, I learnt that by doing the best you can do will make you proud to show people of society what you have achieved and may even motivate you to make and / or help more within society. Lastly, I learnt that impacting one area can impact another. By impacting the environment I impacted society and that this should not be taken lightly and should always be considered prior to, during and when completing a project.

topic: Initiative and the willingness to make decisions in the face of uncertainty
situation: Working as a plumber I received an urgent call on my non working day from a client regarding a burst water pipe.
task_action: Immediately I notified the client to turn the residents' water off at the meter. Upon my arrival at the site I saw water leaking from the bathroom wall through the tiles. I was required to determine the location of the leak within the bathroom wall to begin repairs. First I examined the wall to pinpoint exactly where the water was leaking from. Once located I used a specialised thermal imagery camera to inspect the area for further water damage. This allowed me to see hot water leaking from the pipe in a rough area within the tiled wall. Next I made the decision to carefully remove the tiles in the surrounding area. Using a jack hammer and chisel I removed the render to reveal two copper pipes. Once properly exposed, I assessed the damage to the copper pipe within the wall. The 15mm copper hot water pipe had split causing the leak. I proceeded to fix the damage pipe by cutting and removing the section of split copper. Once removed I cleaned and prepped the copper within the wall to replace the split section. With my specialised crimping tool I reconnected the piping with copper crimp sockets making the joins water tight and secure. Subsequently the water supply was turned back on to check for leaks ensuring the problem was resolved.
result: Through this display of initiative and willingness to make decisions during uncertainty I was able to successfully locate the cause of the issue and provide a carefully considered solution. In doing so there was no further damage to the property. In conjunction providing an efficient response with minimal disruption to the client guaranteed a positive experience for all parties involved.
pfr: The emergency call out from the client was concerning, specifically the feeling of not knowing the damage caused to the scene prior to my arrival. By reacting quickly to the situation and notifying the client to turn the water off to the whole residents whilst on the phone I knew I was reducing the risk of further water damage to the property which provided a sense of calm. Once I arrived it felt important to make sure the client was aware of the necessary process to find the leak as this involved removing tiles and using power tools in their bathroom. In addition I was worried about how much damage I would cause when locating the leak. However using the thermal imagery camera made me feel confident on where to start removing tiles and render. Similarly the use of drop sheets increased my feelings of confidence by protecting the floor tiles and surrounding bathroom fixtures preventing further damage. Overall I felt happy with the outcome.
learning: This experience taught me the importance of being ready in any circumstances to receive an emergency call out even on my non-working days. Responding promptly saved the client money and demonstrated our company values to provide a professional service, even outside of standard business hours. In conjunction I learnt the importance of explaining the process to the client to ensure they understood why I was required to cause damage to their bathroom. Providing the client with comfort and confidence in my abilities. The positive result of this experience has given me confidence in my ability to show initiative when making decisions.

topic: The impact of engineering on society and the environment
situation: We were required to design a 4-bit binary adder for Aurdino on TinkerCad. Each LED light represented a bit, and the motherboard would add the bits entered upon the press of a button and show the results in decimal and hexadecimal values—the project aimed to demonstrate the practical application of digital logic and programming concepts in hardware design.
task_action: This project was an individual assessment. To achieve this objective, we extensively studied the fundamental principles of binary addition. We then specified the 4-bit binary adder prerequisites, encompassing the input/output setups and operating criteria. Using the powerful tools of Tinkercad and Arduino IDE, we constructed the circuit architecture by strategically selecting and arranging the essential components within the virtual environment. This included input switches, output display LEDs, and Arduino microcontroller boards. We rigorously simulated the circuit before proceeding with the coding process to ensure its correct operation. With the Arduino IDE, we meticulously programmed and debugged the code to gain complete control over the binary addition process. We implemented functions to execute binary addition, which included mechanisms to manage carry-over bits and identify issues such as overflow or underflow. The code was optimised for efficiency and accuracy, considering the limited resources of the Arduino microcontroller.
result: We achieved the effective execution of a 4-bit binary adder by utilizing Arduino microcontrollers and software-based algorithms. We were able to check the accuracy of the addition process and see the output using virtual LEDs in the Tinkercad simulation, which did a good job of showing how the binary adder worked. We thoroughly tested the binary adder using a range of input combinations to verify its durability and dependability. The utilization of software-based methods obviated the necessity for tangible logic gates, hence streamlining the circuit design and diminishing the hardware's intricacy. In addition, we recorded the coding methodologies and algorithms employed in the project to disseminate expertise and perspectives to those interested in digital circuitry design and programming for embedded systems. The Tinkercad simulation functioned as an instructional instrument, offering a practical learning opportunity for students and amateurs investigating Arduino-based projects. In summary, the project showcased the flexibility and capabilities of Arduino microcontrollers to carry out intricate computational tasks without relying on additional hardware components. The demonstration exhibited the effectiveness of software-based solutions in designing digital circuits and emphasised the possibilities of simulation tools such as Tinkercad in creating and evaluating electronic systems.
pfr: At first, the challenge of constructing a 4-bit binary adder using Arduino without employing logic gates seemed intimidating. As an individual with expertise in conventional circuit design, I find the prospect of depending exclusively on software algorithms for binary addition alien and daunting. As I immersed myself more in the project and began investigating coding methodologies and algorithms, I experienced a surge of enthusiasm and curiosity. The idea of performing binary addition only through software manipulation piqued my curiosity and motivated me to investigate novel approaches to engineering challenges. While working on the project, I experienced irritation and anxiety, especially during the debugging process when I found problems and unpredictable behaviour in the code. Nevertheless, these hurdles proved to be excellent learning experiences, compelling me to enhance my coding abilities and cultivate a more profound comprehension of the complexities of binary arithmetic and microcontroller programming.
learning: This project gave me a profound respect for the beneficial effects engineering can have on the environment and society, particularly when combined with such adaptable instruments as Arduino microcontrollers. It highlighted the value of imagination and adaptability in engineering and demonstrated how novel ideas might result from nonconformist thinking. The project also highlighted the significance of software-driven solutions in contemporary engineering. Through the use of software, we can tackle difficult problems with more adaptability and scalability, increasing the likelihood of finding long-term solutions. I plan to adopt an interdisciplinary approach in the future, fusing hardware and software to create cutting-edge solutions that meet society's and the environment's requirements. I'll continue to approach things with a curious and experimental perspective, understanding that real innovation comes from taking chances and pushing the envelope.

situation: I was involved in the coordination and implementation of an international motorsport drift school as well as the maintenance and modification of approximately 40 individual customers vehicles for a quarterly event.
task_action: As part of the management involved in the coordinating of both school and customer vehicles, our role was to ensure that both school vehicles and customers vehicles adhered to strict safety regulations, as well as any other requested maintenance or modifications were carried out in the time frame required and in accordance with the rules and regulations of the venue holding the event. Action: Due to the number of vehicles that required attention, we implemented strict deadlines for both requests for maintenance and requests for modification. Our initial focus was on school vehicles for both modification and maintenance, as they had priority, followed by customer vehicle maintenance including modifications that were required for said vehicles to meet the standard to compete in the event. Everything else then followed. This allowed for a structured list of vehicles to be completed with given deadlines and timeframes for each vehicle including the required work to be carried out.

This often lead to vehicles being not completed in entirety, but instead to a level that allowed the vehicle to compete in the event even in its incomplete state.
learning: While effort was put into best prioritizing each vehicle, it was often difficult to differentiate between two vehicles and deciding on what work should be carried out first. This experience showed me that although best efforts were put into the organization, often we are met with challenges that simply cannot allow us to achieve 100%, and that we are often required to sacrifice in one aspect or another. result: * ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT: We successfully developed a water filtration system that reduced environmental impact by 40% compared to existing products, due to its use of sustainable materials and efficient manufacturing processes. * SOCIAL IMPACT: The system was affordable and easy to use, significantly improving access to clean water in underprivileged communities. Working with my team, we navigated each stage methodically, and the collective effort and diverse perspectives made the task manageable and even inspiring. Seeing the positive impact our work had on communities reinforced the importance of our mission and the potential of engineering to drive meaningful change.
learning: This experience taught me the power of structured, merit-based decision-making and the value of collaboration in tackling complex problems. By systematically evaluating each design against clear criteria, we ensured that our final product was both effective and sustainable. I also learned that the "best" solution is always relative to the specific constraints and needs it addresses. This realization has deepened my appreciation for the nuanced nature of engineering design and the importance of adaptability and responsiveness to feedback. Moving forward, I will prioritize structured decision-making and open collaboration in my projects, always considering the broader social and environmental impacts of our work. This approach will not only enhance the quality and relevance of our solutions but also ensure that we remain aligned with our commitment to sustainability and social responsibility.

Additionally, I sought support and guidance from mentors and peers, seeking advice on effective time management strategies and seeking assistance when needed.
result: Implementing the STAR framework significantly improved my ability to manage time and resources effectively. By clearly defining tasks and setting priorities, I became more focused and productive, completing assignments and projects in a timely manner. I experienced reduced stress levels and a greater sense of control over my workload. Furthermore, I noticed improvements in my academic performance, as I was able to dedicate more time to studying and understanding course material. Overall, the result of applying the STAR framework was a more balanced and fulfilling student experience, with enhanced productivity and better utilization of resources.

situation: For my second engineering workshop: Machining, I was to spend each lesson working through a schematic type diagram, using aluminium I measured, marked, cut, folded, etc, various pieces to create a metal toolbox, as the major project. task_action: It became more and more obvious that If I wanted to complete the toolbox on time, to get as many marks as possible, I needed to figure out someway of working on the project outside of class. As such I eventually learned that the workshop is available to students throughout the week. On the Friday morning the week before the due date I came in early to the workshop outside of class hours and managed to fit in 3 hours worth of progress, the same length of time of each workshop lesson.
result: Because the situation was so urgent, I managed to be flexible enough to find the time necessary to put in those few extra hours between class. pfr: As time went on it became increasingly frustrating, realising how far behind I was in terms of progress, and especially compared to most other students who were already assembling the box as I was just starting on my last two pieces. learning: Often, I feel that putting in extra effort to catch up on work when in a position where I am behind where I should be is all in vein and will not change the result anyway, which is a poor attitude based on prior experience. situation: We recently encountered a customer who operated a manufacturing facility experiencing issues with its wastewater treatment system. The plant had an outdated and underperforming wastewater treatment system. This was causing regulatory and environmental problems due to its ineffective treatment capabilities.

Then we examined innovative technology and best practices in the wastewater treatment industry. We focused on methods that require minimal energy, chemicals, and waste. Based on our assessments, we recommended a multi-pronged approach that included investing in the company’s treatment plants to incorporate state-of-the-art equipment such as membrane bioreactors and advanced oxidation systems. The company was also recommended to implement recycling programs. Other process improvements were generated to enhance resource recovery and reduce waste. In the implementation stage, we worked closely with the company’s technical staff to ensure the proper setup and operation of the new systems and processes. Training and support were provided to help the staff adapt to the changes and to improve the systems’ performance over time. All these measures led to a significant reduction in the company’s waste footprint and the diversion of substantial amounts of recyclable materials
result: Our sustainable wastewater treatment solution significantly benefits to both the company and the environment. The company saved water, electricity and chemicals, leading to increased production efficiency and lower operating costs. Furthermore, the new treatment plant enabled a considerable reduction of pollutants discharged into nature which helped preserve the nearby natural ecosystems and fulfilled legal regulations. In summary, our solution addressed pressing environmental concerns and contributed to corporate sustainability.
