situation: During this semester, I was given the task of creating an IOT tea maker for a client, who had only a vague idea of what they wanted. This task was an individual task, but we were informed that working collaboratively would increase our chances at being successful in this task.
task_action: The task was to define the client's needs and transform their vague requirements into a new, innovative design. The goal was to design an IOT tea maker using core engineering principles that met the client's expectations. The client's requirements included internet-based access, the ability to share tea designs and recipes with friends, and scheduling tea preparation to their preferences, and more. Effective communication was crucial between my group of fellow engineering students, as we all belonged to different disciplines of engineering, We could all bounce ideas off of each other that aligned with our discipline, and that would allow everyone else to gain a new perspective on how to tackle this task. This ensured a cohesive and comprehensive design of the IOT Tea Maker. To Address this challenge, I suggested we all join a google Doc where we would be able to write down our ideas without being spoken over or ignored, and at the end we could all talk through our ideas and explain our thought process. By doing this, we had thought of numerous ideas, which we would then evaluate based on a criteria of complexity, how well it would service the customer and how feasible it would be. I actively communicated with the group to refine these ideas, ensuring that each concept was thoroughly discussed and analysed. I also made sure that everyone felt included and that no one's ideas were being put on the back burner.
result: Through successful communication with engineering students from different disciplines, we significantly enhanced our individual designs of the IOT tea maker. My final design incorporated a user-friendly interface, automated brewing schedules, and connectivity features that allowed users to control the tea maker via a smartphone app. This collaborative approach not only improved the design quality but also ensured that the final product met the client's needs comprehensively.
pfr: Initially, the task of creating an IOT tea maker for a client who had such vague requirements felt overwhelming. The uncertainty around the client's needs and the complexity of integrating various unknown engineering principles added to this fear that I will not be able to successfully complete this task to the best of my capabilities. This had made me very anxious and worried during the early weeks of the task. However, I was also excited to learn about new engineering concepts and design this IOT Tea Maker. Being told that, despite it being a solo task, we were encouraged to communicate with a group had me feeling slightly relieved, as I could ask for clarification on any concepts I had trouble understanding. Despite me being a very shy and timid person, I had to break the ice with the 8 people who were sitting at my table during the first week and talk to them about the idea I had of us collaborating together and sharing a document where we could write down our ideas in class and collaborate together. During this moment, I demonstrated strength in my ability to communicate with others, despite it being something I had to push myself out of my comfort zone to do. As we continued to work together, I had felt a sense of satisfaction and relief. The idea of sharing a google doc had become a powerful brainstorming and collaborative tool where we could all contribute our ideas without fear of being wrong or ignored. Seeing all the different perspectives on how to tackle certain problems when we were discussing ideas was amazing. Yet, there were moments of frustration when conflicts arose or when some ideas seemed unfeasible. Navigating these challenges required patience and empathy, which sometimes felt emotionally taxing but ultimately rewarding.
learning: This experience had been an eye-opener as it showcased the effectiveness of communication and structured collaboration. I had realised that communicating with a group of like minded people on a task can turn the task from a seemingly overwhelming one to a more manageable one. By being in an environment where everyone's ideas were valued and group discussions were prioritised, we could fully utilise our individual strengths. Communication as a skill is crucial, as it helped me realise that the best solutions often came from collective effort rather than individual brilliance. The various perspectives from different engineering disciplines helped develop our design and helped us better meet the clients wacky needs. This lesson taught me the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and approaching problems with an open mind, ready to see the problem from a different perspective. For future projects, I will aim to openly communicate with others and promote inclusivity, encouraging broad and unique ideas to be discussed. Additionally, I can work on improving my conflict resolution skills, handling differing opinions in a respectful manner, and maintaining a positive work environment where everyone feels safe. Overall, the ability to effectively communicate within a group has allowed me to appreciate the power of teamwork and build my communication skills, focusing on maintaining mutual respect within the group. These skills can be carried into my future prospects, in terms of group projects and working in a professional environment.

We are a three-person team, and this assignment is a vital part of our coursework. Given the short turnaround time and the fact that none of us had any prior expertise designing gearboxes, the problem is substantial.
task_action: Designing and building a working gearbox that could show durability and efficiency under a range of loads was our job. For the competition, we had to follow certain design guidelines and incorporate our gearbox into a bigger mechanical system. Due to time and budget restrictions, the task's intricacy required a thorough grasp of gear ratios, material selection, and assembly processes. Our group used a calculated strategy to address this problem. We started by breaking the project up into smaller, more doable jobs according to our unique skills and interests. In order to maximize our gearbox layout, I took the initiative to investigate gear design concepts and simulation tools. My partners concentrated on locating supplies, fabricating parts, and carrying out practical testing in the meantime. We met on a regular basis to discuss issues, exchange updates, and modify our plans in light of new information and disappointments. We were transparent in our communication and flexible in our design modifications in response to feedback and testing conducted in the real world.
result: Our group's perseverance and efforts are paying off. Even with unanticipated obstacles like wrong calculations, we are manage to design a gearbox that promises to outperform our first performance estimates. In addition, the project is teaching us important lessons about problem-solving, collaboration, and project management. This experience showcases clear how crucial it is to be persistent, quick thinking, and flexible in order to accomplish challenging engineering goals in cooperative settings and under pressure.
pfr: Starting the task of building a gearbox with my group felt a bit like taking a leap into something unknown at first. Given that none of us had any experience with designing gearboxes, the task appeared quite difficult. The impending deadline added to the pressure we were under. But as we began to approach the issue carefully and break it down into manageable pieces, my feelings of uneasiness started to give way to a feeling of purpose and determination. We were able to work together to overcome the complexity, and as a result, every phase of the decision-making process became more organized and clear. Seeing our group come together and agree on design decisions based on project objectives and established merits was comforting.
learning: I now have a clearer understanding of the value of well-organized decision-making and productive teamwork as a result of this experience. Our strategy, in which choices were taken on the basis of objective merits and careful evaluation of limitations, worked well to ensure group consensus and hastened our development. I discovered that there is rarely a "best design" that works for all difficult engineering projects; instead, a design's efficacy is greatly influenced by the particular problem statement and the restrictions that go along with it. My viewpoint on project management and problem-solving has expanded as a result of this insight. I plan to put what I've learned into practice by giving structured decision-making procedures top priority in any future group projects. I think it's important to have specific goals, define evaluation standards, and encourage candid communication among team members. Adopting this strategy, in my opinion, will enable us to make decisions more quickly and effectively—even when faced with difficult projects. This experience has shown how crucial it is to have persistence, flexibility, and teamwork in order to overcome challenges and accomplish challenging engineering goals.

These persona's would be viable customers for a product solution to this pain point. This allowed me to more accurately cater my app using feedback. My team, consisting of five members, had diverse ideas about the drone's design, leading to initial disagreements on the direction we should take.
task_action: My role involved coordinating our team's efforts to merge our individual design ideas into a cohesive CAD model and then preparing a compelling oral presentation that showcased our design process, challenges, and the innovative features of our drone. The ultimate goal was to communicate our project's value effectively and demonstrate our collaborative and technical skills. We discussed potential features, materials, and technologies that could enhance our drone's flight time. After consolidating our ideas, we divided the work based on individual strengths—two members focused on the aerodynamics in the CAD software, two worked on the presentation visuals and script, and I oversaw the entire project to ensure cohesion and adherence to our timeline. Together, we iterated on our CAD model, integrating feedback from practice presentations in front of peers.
result: Our collaborative approach resulted in a highly innovative drone design, featuring lightweight materials and an aerodynamic shape that significantly extended flight times. The oral presentation was well-received by our classmates and instructors, highlighting not only the technical aspects of our design but also our team's ability to work together, solve problems, and communicate effectively. Our project was praised for its clear presentation, innovative design, and the comprehensive understanding of CAD tools we demonstrated. This experience not only solidified my skills in CAD design and teamwork but also underscored the importance of communication in engineering projects.
pfr: When we first embarked on the CAD design project for the new drone, I felt a mixture of excitement and apprehension. The excitement stemmed from the opportunity to apply my skills and creativity to something tangible and potentially groundbreaking. However, apprehension crept in due to the diverse opinions within the team on the direction of the project. Initially, the differing viewpoints led to some frustration, as it seemed challenging to find a common ground. The task ahead appeared formidable, not because of the complexity of the design itself but due to the need to unify our team's vision. Throughout the brainstorming sessions and collaboration, however, I discovered the value in each team member's perspective, realizing that our diversity was not a barrier but a strength that enriched our final design.
learning: The experience taught me several key lessons about teamwork, communication, and problem-solving in design projects. Firstly, I learned the importance of open communication and active listening. By truly listening to and considering each idea, we were able to integrate the best aspects of each proposal, leading to a more innovative and comprehensive design. This process underscored the notion that great ideas can come from anywhere, and a collaborative approach can harness these ideas into a coherent and effective solution. Moreover, I gained insight into the significance of flexibility and adaptability in teamwork. Rather than clinging to my initial ideas, I learned to be flexible, adapting my contributions to better fit the evolving design and team needs. This adaptability was crucial in overcoming obstacles and pushing the project forward. In future projects, I will act differently by proactively fostering an environment of open communication and respect for diverse ideas from the outset. I will also prioritize building a structured yet flexible project framework that allows for the seamless integration of different perspectives. This experience has taught me that the synergy of a well-coordinated team can transform individual ideas into innovations greater than the sum of their parts. Lastly, I've come to appreciate the process of reflection itself as a powerful tool for personal and professional growth, enabling me to approach future challenges with confidence and a more collaborative mindset.

situation: I was a part of a team tasked with planning and constructing a Rube Goldberg machine in my first year of engineering. However, the unit was being held online at the time due to the COVID-19 pandemic. This caused many difficulties as the collaborative nature of constructing such a complicated contraption required hands-on interaction and real-time problem-solving, which was not possible through the online environment. Even though we were able to make a strong start with each team member responsible for a certain section of the machine, it became apparent that certain design flaws were causing disruptions. As each member was working and individually constructing their own part, it was difficult to create synchronisation between components.
task_action: To overcome these obstacles, the team collectively organised virtual brainstorming sessions and established clear communication channels to ensure updates on progress. At times, the work had to be broken down into more manageable tasks. One of the biggest pain points was the fact that we were doing the project online, and it was hard to join individual parts together to create a functioning machine. To address this, the team decided to come on campus with individual components and equipment and construct the machine there. By doing this, we were able to clearly pinpoint the areas that were causing problems and work together to solve them. We maintained these regular in-person check-ins to ensure everyone stayed on track and that any issues were instantly addressed. Furthermore, we utilised digital modelling software and shared online platforms to visualise and troubleshoot the integration of individual components, ensuring compatibility and smooth operation when assembled.
result: Despite the challenges posed by the online work environment, my team and I successfully constructed a functioning Rube Goldberg machine. By utilising technology and maintaining open communication, we were able to collaborate effectively and overcome the limitations. The final result was not only evidence of our creativity but also demonstrated our ability to adapt and thrive in challenging circumstances.
pfr: Initially, navigating and trying to approach the project in a way that would be successful proved to be a difficult task. The online environment felt extremely overwhelming, and there was no sense of direction. We were faced with a lot of issues that made the entire team frustrated as well as tense, as everyone questioned whether we would even be able to complete the project successfully or not. However, as we began to tackle the problem systematically and communicate effectively as a team, I found a sense of reassurance and determination. Despite the obstacles, there was a shared commitment among team members to overcome the challenges and succeed in our goal.
learning: This experience taught me the importance of adaptability and resilience in the face of adversity. It also taught me how crucial it is to identify pain points before taking the correct steps to solve them. The online environment posed limitations, but it also made us think outside the box and find alternate solutions. The decision to come together in person to construct the machine was pivotal in our progress, and we were able to solve several issues. This experience also demonstrated the power of technology to facilitate collaboration. Moving forward, I have gained a deeper appreciation for the value of face-to-face interaction and hands-on problem-solving. In future projects, I will prioritise early and frequent communication, leveraging both digital tools and in-person meetings to ensure effective collaboration. Furthermore, I understand the importance of flexibility and adaptability in responding to unexpected challenges, recognising that innovation often arises from constraints. Overall, this experience has reinforced the importance of perseverance and teamwork in achieving success, even in the most challenging circumstances.

situation: My journey as a full-time engineering student concurrently working part-time as a teaching academic at the university exemplified a demanding challenge. The dual commitment required me to juggle rigorous engineering coursework with the responsibility of assisting other students academically. This dual role was both an honour and a colossal task. The primary challenge arose from the conflicting schedules between my classes, study time, and teaching hours. Often, these commitments overlapped, leading to stress and the potential compromise of my academic performance and my ability to effectively support my students.
task_action: The critical task ahead of me was to devise a strategy that ensured my success as a student and as a teaching academic. The goal was to achieve a balance that would not only allow me to excel academically but also to fulfil my teaching responsibilities with the dedication and effectiveness they deserved. This required creating a flexible schedule that accommodated the intensive periods of my coursework, such as exams and project deadlines, without neglecting the needs of the students I was teaching. ACTION: To tackle this challenge, I embarked on a multifaceted approach. First, I initiated transparent discussions with my academic advisors and the department head, laying out the specifics of my situation. I proposed a flexible teaching schedule that could be adjusted during critical academic periods. Recognizing the need for efficiency, I also adopted digital tools such as Trello and iCal, even Notion and platforms to create online tutorials and forums for my students, ensuring they had continuous access to learning resources. This digital shift not only allowed me to manage my time more effectively but also catered to the diverse needs of my students. Moreover, I dedicated time each week to meticulously plan out my activities, prioritizing tasks based on urgency and importance. This disciplined approach to time management was pivotal in navigating through the busiest periods of the semester.
result: The outcome of these concerted efforts was highly positive in my first year of teaching in higher education. Proactive steps are taken to manage the dual roles effectively. The flexibility in my teaching schedule during peak academic times was instrumental in maintaining my academic performance. Furthermore, the digital resources were met with positive feedback from students, who found them to be valuable supplements to traditional learning methods. This experience not only underscored the importance of adaptability and proactive problem-solving but also highlighted the value of effective communication and digital innovation in educational settings. The skills and insights gained from this experience are invaluable, reinforcing my ability to manage complex situations and drive positive outcomes in both academic and professional environments.

situation: In my software engineering course (COMP4060), my team and I were tasked with creating and analysing a real-life scenario that highlighted ethical challenges in software development, particularly those involving user privacy and data protection. Our hypothetical situation involves a corporation that created an application that unintentionally acquired more user data than disclosed, including sensitive personal information, without the users' explicit agreement. This circumstance reflected real-world difficulties, highlighting the intricacies of ethical decision-making in the technology business.
task_action: Our goal was to provide a solution that addressed the ethical, technical, and social responsibilities involved in the case. We wanted not only to address the existing situation but also to prevent future instances from happening. The solution needed adherence to ethical standards, regulatory compliance, and data protection best practices. ACTION: We began our strategy by performing an extensive study on data privacy legislation, ethical software development principles, and industry standards for user data security alongside case studies related to the topic of utilising/trading customers’ data in illegal ways. Some of those included the recent allegations of OpenAI using illegally collected data to train their AI and Facebook’s history of illegally collecting data without its user’s consent. Based on our results, we started a brainstorming session for 20 minutes aimed at building a multidimensional solution to the problem. Our proposed solution comprised technical measures to protect user data that range from better sourcing analytics and providing ethical training to the development team, to a transparent communication approach to regain consumer trust such as publicising how and what data is collected and used and making public statements regularly regarding the company’s customer security and data privacy, and an internal audit of data-gathering processes. In addition, we proposed that employees receive regular ethical training in order to establish a culture of responsibility and honesty.
result: The initiative resulted in an extensive strategy that not only addressed the issue of unethical data collection but also laid the groundwork for long-term ethical procedures within the organisation. While our method was praised for its thoroughness and practicality, the process caused me to think hard about my ideals and obligations as a prospective software developer. I understood the vital need to incorporate ethical considerations into all stages of software development, from design to deployment. It strengthened my opinion that transparency, user permission, and personal data protection are non-negotiable values in technology. Furthermore, the experiment demonstrated the importance of ongoing ethical education and a strong ethical culture in preventing wrongdoing. This realisation has reaffirmed my dedication to prioritising ethical standards in my professional trajectory over profits or other means, ensuring that my activities benefit the tech industry and society as a whole.
pfr: I was both excited and nervous about participating in this discussion. The difficulty of addressing such a complicated ethical issue in the technology business was out of my comfort zone, but it also provided an opportunity to delve deeply into the complexities of software creation beyond mere writing code. However, as we advanced, I became increasingly interested in exploring and comprehending the ethical components that underlay our digital world. The process of brainstorming solutions with my team was especially informative, providing varied viewpoints that improved our final approach. I felt accomplished as we devised a strategy that addressed not only the technical and ethical components of the issue but also showed our shared commitment to social responsibility.
learning: This experience has helped shape my perception of the importance of ethics in software development. It emphasised the importance of the need to evaluate the broader impact of technological solutions on consumers and society. The realisation that technology is not value-neutral but is inextricably linked to ethical considerations has altered my outlook on my future position as a software engineer. I've learned the importance of incorporating ethical decision-making throughout the development process, from basic design to final deployment. This thought has taught me the value of openness, user permission, and data protection as core concepts in technology. Moving forward, I intend to apply these values to my professional work, advocate for ethical practices, and continue to educate myself about the increasing difficulties at the confluence of technology and ethics. The knowledge obtained from this project will influence my actions, ensuring that I help design technology that respects user rights and supports a fair and just digital society.

situation: I NEEDED TO COOPERATE WITH MY COWORKERS AND COMMUNICATE WITH CUSTOMERS TO SAFELY RUN A WORKSITE WHICH HAS CONSTANT TRAFFIC FLOW. AT KIMBRIKI ENVIRONMENTAL ENTERPRISES, I ALONG WITH MY COWORKERS CONTROL THE WASTE DISPOSAL OF ALL VEHICLES. WITH 1200 VEHICLES ON OUR SITE OVER THE COURSE OF THE 10 HOUR SHIFT THERE IS A CRUCIAL ROLE IN THE COMMUNICATION WITHIN THE TRAFFIC CONTROL ASPECT TO KEEP BOTH WORKERS AND CUSTOMERS SAFE. COMMUNICATION IS VITAL IN HAVING A SAFE WORKPLACE. COMMUNICATION IS CONSISTENT IN ALL WORKPLACES, WHETHER IN AN OFFICE OR ON A WORKSITE. CLEAR, SHORT AND UNIVERSAL COMMUNICATION ALLOWS FOR MESSAGES TO BE PHYSICALLY OR VERBALLY CONVEYED WITH EASE WHETHER THEY ARE INSTRUCTIONS OR WARNINGS.
task_action: Implementing meetings and training allow employees to be on the same page and create a minimum skill level. Having employees on the same page is one of the most important aspects in regards to communication because these workers will have similar unified verbal communications or sign language. Dealing with vehicle traffic flow requires my coworkers and I to have simple sign languages like a straight arm with palm up facing traffic for a ‘STOP’ or an extended arm with a pushing motion to the ground to communicate ‘SLOW DOWN’ to customers to maximise understanding and decrease the risk of injury or damage. Furthermore, messages between coworkers with short concise phrases over a two way radio system allow for there to be little confusion and increased radio silence. This is particularly important incase of an emergency. For example, a coworker can quickly inform the site coordinator that there has been a dumping of hazardous waste like unwrapped asbestos or chemicals because there is not unnecessary noise on the radios. In doing so customers can be properly protected, and the waste can be cleaned up efficiently.
result: The result was being able run a worksite which has clear communications between coworkers and customers, which leads to a heavily reduced risk level for a high-risk workplace. Workplaces with high levels of effective communications create a nearly risk free environment.
pfr: In a customer-facing role with my main responsibility being the safety of others' lives as well as my own, I felt very overwhelmed with the pressure of keeping people safe. Working at Kimbriki Environmental Enterprises, I am constantly surrounded by different vehicles ranging from sedans and suvs to forklifts and loaders. Although the various sizes of the vehicles, the operations of safety are the same. Traffic control is the most important factor and this requires the soft skill of communication. This skill is crucial because one incorrect hand gesture or a lack of specificity with instructions could lead to serious harm. As a result this potential harm created an anxiety which only settled with the aid of my coworkers and the high levels of communication we installed. With Kimbriki being open to the public, I am working with all ages, diverse nationalities and of people of all abilities. This poses a challenge with assuming a gesture or direction is straightforward and that every person would understand the instruction. However this is not the case and this can create dangerous habits if assuming that all people have the same understanding as myself. Sometimes it is people's first time at this specific site or first time disposing of waste or English is not their first language. I sometimes struggled with this concept as I would give people instructions and as they drove off they seemed still unsure or would get lost. I felt embarrassed and I questioned why this was happening. After seeking feedback from fellow coworkers on my communication skills, I realised I needed to simplify my communication skills using more universal ways of communicating including smaller words and more hand gestures.
learning: I was intrigued with how this soft skill of communication could be so effective by simplifying and reducing unnecessary communication. This realisation has dramatically improved my work, as I use less words, people are happier because they are given correct, concise directions and there is a very low risk level. topic: TOPIC/S: Throughout the first half of the semester, within my team, we have learnt how to effectively use data-driven decision making and create new solution concepts in order to obtain the best outcome possible that fits the requirements and then goes beyond. The main implementation of these skills is our Idea Conveyor Belt. We constructed a way to filter through all of our ideas, whether they be for sustainability, aesthetics, mechanics or other aspects of the Rube Goldberg Machine where we will be planting a seed. This way, we can use what we’ve seen from past experiences and adapt our ideas to make new decisions and see what worked best to make new solutions.
situation: For our conceptual design of the Rube Goldberg Machine, we needed to throw a lot of ideas onto the table. Gathering as many as we could, would increase the chances of reaching higher quality ideas and being able to do things like merge solutions to create a hybrid that would otherwise not be good enough for our project.
task_action: We wanted to create a working design that flowed well and was sustainable while also having creative aspects to it. Our group was going to put ideas out for everyone to see and then choose some that they wanted to do and put them together to form their two events. This way, everyone would feel like they were contributing to the final design and we could easily come up with something. We realised that the ideas we had come up with were too complicated to be executed and, although they looked good, we needed to tone it back a bit to make better working events. To ensure we finished the work and made it simple, we set individual deadlines for our team members, depending on what they had yet to complete. We also went through each event and allowed the team member running it to explain their ideas before we each gave our feedback on how we thought it would go and specifically working out each detail so that it would be a feasible task.
result: To adapt to our new changes while still keeping the original idea, we decided that we would all make simple events but we could add our own flair. This way, our actions would have a personal touch and feel like our own while still being executable. Our Idea Conveyor Belt means that we can put all our suggestions up for criticism and then filter through using pro/con lists on how they would work and our interest in them. After that, we will modify them to make them more sustainable to suit the theme and our idea of planting a seed.
pfr: Each week, in our pre-workshop meetings, we discuss any problems we’ve had with the project or other team members. We found out that getting everything out in the open works best and it soon showed us that we were feeling somewhat lonely or uncomfortable with how we were working on the Rube Goldberg Machine. Following is how we resolved that issue and created a better way to work together as a team instead of individually as a team. We decided to create a mass group of ideas and concepts and then pick and choose. We collaborated to work out who would go after who and which events we would take before going off separately and planning/executing our own concepts. Personally, it was very encouraging to brainstorm together as we all felt encouraged to present any kind of idea and I didn’t feel judged about what I was saying, or typing into our Miro board, even if I thought that my idea was a little dumb. However, when it came to going home and working on the project, I felt a bit overwhelmed and I didn’t feel like I could go to someone for help with coming up with my events as everyone seemed so independent and like they knew exactly what they were doing. I’ve been in situations before where my group hasn’t worked well together and were at each other’s throats, working individually instead of as a team. Contrastingly, I’ve also worked on individual assessments where I’ve focused too much on being creative and have let myself down when it came to physically carrying out my plan. Using our strategies, our team worked through any problems and made sure everyone could make their event a reality.
learning: Each week, we look at what worked well and what didn’t work well in our previous meetings so that we can adopt the strategies that were clever and get rid of the detrimental ones. For example, we realised that sending each team member out by themselves to work on their actions was not a good idea. Although it seemed like it was at first because we can do what we want, we need help and the problem-solving attitudes of our team members to bounce off of to create the best project. Splitting up isolated us and we often felt a bit helpless because we were only relying on ourselves. We learnt that we need a way to sort through the masses of ideas because we are good at coming up with them, but we need to work harder on actually picking out ones that will work. In the future, we can use our Idea Conveyor Belt and various ways of filtering like working out the advantages and disadvantages of a particular event and using online tools to share with our group exactly how they will work, using drawings for example. I also learnt to start sharing my problems or any issues I’ve encountered because I know that my group is ever willing to help me out and we can solve the problems as team, which is the reason we were put together for this project.

situation: Within the subject of ENGG2050 we were provided an assignment where I needed to make a consumer a product according to the following wants: These are their major wants * I want an Internet based Tea Maker * I want to wake up to tea, just the way I like it * I want to come home to tea, just the way I like it. These are more minor wants * I want to share my tea style with my friends * I want to have friends * I prefer different teas depending on the time of day. * I like to experiment with new teas that my friends recommend * I want to rate different tea styles
task_action: * _Idea Generation:_ When proceeding with idea generation I took into consideration the consumers needs and wants. I focused on the major wants and began sketching concepts to give myself a standard of the machine I was wanting. In this portion of the innovation process I needed to tick off the consumers minor needs but in some cases avoided them completely. I primarily avoided them as I did not ask the right questions when I was able to. * _Preparation:_ Within this phase, I began to develop my sketches more and more. Moving from sketches into rendered design and real world application processes and installation. I struggled within this area as I did not account for the real-world consequences of certain components being next to each other would entail. For example, having Milk next to the hot water system. * _Innovation: _As the task required innovation within the tea making industry, I began to research into differing ways for tea to be made while avoiding contamination of other tea ingredients into different tea types. I opted for a system flush function which would drain the previously used tea out of the extraction pipes and would remove the used leaves or bags. However, coming up with a functioning system which would avoiding: 1. injuring the consumer, 2. detecting when there is no tea cup under the dispenser, and 3. find a way for there to be tea automatically made after the system flush without human input. I struggled to find a system which would work. I then moved from that segment, due to lack of idea generation for the solution, of the project to the modularity which I wanted the machine to have for easy of used and cleaning purposes. This segment was not difficult and was intentionally designed so that certain segments could be bought after the machine if parts failed. In completing that segment, I moved back to the system flush and auto tea function. In stepping away from the problem for a while I gave my self a refresh to the idea and opted for a system which would make a tea push the cup to the left using a grated track system and flush the system then insert the next cup on the track system. The grated track system allows for the flushed water/tea to fall into a catching pan which needs to be changed every week. * _Testing and Iterations/Monitoring and Evaluation: _As the project did not require for the product to be produced this segment of the innovation process could not be fulfilled.
result: As previously stated in task/action I struggled to come up with a suitable solution to a problem which I faced. By taking step back from the solution process and moving my mind to another problem I allowed myself to effectively design the product. As such I considered most of the needs and wants of the consumer. HOWEVER, I neglected the friends aspect of the system and only focused on the different teas being made.
pfr: The initial task seemed simple at first. As I progressed into the project however, it began to become more complex as certain aspects needed to be considered and focused on. I struggled at points to innovate new ideas to allow for the needs and wants to be met and this did make it more difficult to complete the task to the standard i was hoping for. The final result did meet the requirements of the task, but I did not feel happy with the resulting design. In hindsight I would break down the needs more deeply and offer solutions for the more broken down aspects instead of trying to approach it from such a large scale.
learning: Within this project I learnt the process of innovation and the step required to successfully output a product to a high quality. I was also forced to learn how to more deeply consider the conceptual aspect of design. In doing so I will, in the future, consider the process more deeply and focus on aspects more carefully in order to achieve a better result than I did in this project.

situation: During my current Systems Engineering and Design Thinking course, one of the assignments was the A4 infographic. This assignment consisted in the creation of an infographic to explain a key concept from the textbook that I have learnt during this session. I chose Human Factors in Usability Design.
task_action: . My goal was to create an engaging and informative infographic that clearly conveyed the importance of human factors in usability design. I needed to ensure that the infographic structure had three sections: · An abstraction level · An implementation level · Interesting examples The methods I used to create the infographic were the following: RESEARCH: I conducted a thorough research to understand the definition of Human Factors in Usability Design and the main methodologies used to achieve it. I listed the definition and the main methodologies used as my _abstraction layer_. Similarly, I conducted my research for the implementation level. There is a significant number of ways to implement the Human Factors in Usability Design. I have chosen six methodologies which, in my opinion, are the ones most used by commercial entities that provide Usability Design services. These six methodologies formed my _implementation layer_. SELECTION CRITERIA CREATED AND USED I found many interesting examples and it was difficult to make choices. I used three selection criteria to ensure my examples were relevant and impactful: · Innovative approach · Impact on Users on global scale · Aesthetic Appeal Using the above criteria my selection consisted of 13 examples. These examples formed my _interesting examples layer._ BRAINSTORMING: I started by brainstorming different ways to present the information, focusing on clarity and engagement. I explored various themes, color schemes, and layouts. DESIGN ITERATION: I created multiple drafts, experimenting with different visual elements like location on the page, graphics, and fonts.
result: As a result of these efforts, I submitted the A4 infographic. In my opinion, the infographic effectively communicated complex concepts in an accessible and visually appealing way. Working on the A4 infographic not only enhanced my conceptual understanding of Human Factors in Usability Design but also strengthened my skills in creative problem-solving, visual communication, and user-centered design. It was a valuable exercise in integrating technical knowledge with conceptual design thinking principles.
pfr: I am a neurodivergent student (ADHD). I often experience challenges specific to that condition, especially the ones related to the Executive Function. The challenge of planning and completing the A4 infographic was mainly linked to feelings of inadequacy due to my tendency to procrastinate. For this task, I also found the concepts quite new to me and it took me some time to understand their application and their interaction within systems design. The textbook information helped, however I needed to also do additional research which increased the time I spent on finalising the task.
learning: As a result of this experience, I learnt the importance of a structured approach to engineering design and the value of using theoretical information and effective research. I have also developed an increased appreciation of the need for accurate planning ahead of time and ensuring tasks are completed in line with the schedule. I have consolidated my use of the calendar as an essential time management tool with very good results. Another important lesson learnt through this experience was related to the value of communicating concepts using the abstraction level and the implementation level. I have also better understood the value of the infographic as an efficient communication tool. For the future, I will keep a positive frame of mind when studying something new and will definitely use my planning tools and resources to improve my results. I feel that through this experience I have consolidated my approach to studying, working with new concepts and communicating them using a concise format. I will also be better at managing my stress and staying focused on the end goal.

The purpose of our team project was to build a tea-maker machine. Throughout the process of developing the project, I was responsible for recording and taking notes of our each week’s tutorial work and talk to the group members about their tasks. We were given tutorial tasks each week in order to assist the process of developing our product. I was chosen to record and wrap each week’s work done by everyone. As it was group work my communication skill was to be challenged in order to get everyone’s idea correctly and precisely so that our project runs smoothly.
task_action: At first, it was easy for every member to communicate with each other, but as the project went on, I have noticed some of our members being unhappy about their given tasks. When the time came to discuss and brief about the tasks we had a pretty heated debate on wether or not whose idea was better than the other. Specifically on deciding the design of our product, I had proposed my idea and it was brilliant which indeed was at the time to me. However, two of our members argued that their idea was better than mine. It was ridiculous how much time I have spent on the design and someone says it was “not very good”.Though it took some time for me to listen and understand everyone’s point of view, someone had to take charge and end the argument. Action: I stepped in as soon as everyone cooled off after the argument and tried to lighten up the mood by expressing my gratitude on every members contribution, how everyone was involved in the project that they had their own ideas to share. I thought to myself that they wanted the project to be just as much success as I wanted it to be. Also I was part of a team where everyone was doing their best to make it work. I have apologised if I was rude to them by forcing my idea on everyone, and the two of our members have apologized to me for criticizing my work so quickly when I have spent so many time on it. Our group was finally in the mood to actually develop our design ideas, so we have included everyone’s best ideas and finalized our design. I felt so empowered and accomplished though we were not finished with the final product yet. But I had a feeling that it would be good as long as everyone including myself communicate with each other so well that we will be ready to overcome any challenges that we might face.
result: As a result, I have realized how strong communication affects a group’s dynamics and productiveness. I noticed that I struggled with communicating my ideas correctly so that the other person understands it, as well as getting offended my constructive criticism. I could have listened to their points and try improve my design rather than claiming that it was my best work and they shouldn’t judge it. Listening to people and communicating while encouraging everyone else to speak their ideas are the soft skills that I have mostly improved during the project. I am excited to further develop these skills and use it in any team project that I might do in the future. Also, I will be telling this in my job interview how I have strong communication skills that I have been practicing since completing units like this.

I have encouraged everyone to speak one at a time and calmed everyone by letting them know that their ideas were all valid and not to be overlooked. I have simply reminded everyone that we should choose the best points from everyone's ideas and make the whole design on those little good points from everyone. Our design turned out really good, thanks to everyone's contribution.
learning: By leading the discussion and communicating effectively after that argument, I have learned how communication affects the group atmosphere and every member's feelings. Strong communication skills are key to achieving any goal as a team on any project. I will try and improve my communication skills in the future, by participating in more group projects and team settings. I will be a more effective speaker and listener from now on and will use that skill to be someone who is fun, enjoyable, encouraging, empowering to be in one group with.

situation: In our mechanical engineering design unit, we were tasked with designing a gearbox for a crane, a crucial component that would impact the crane's efficiency and safety. The project required close collaboration among team members, each with varying opinions on the design approach due to differences in technical understanding and priorities.
task_action: As the team leader, my role was to guide the design process, ensure all technical requirements were met, and maintain team cohesion. This involved managing differing opinions to find the most efficient design solution while ensuring that each team member felt valued and heard. ACTION: To address the team's diverse views, I organized structured brainstorming sessions where each member could present their design ideas and the rationale behind them. To promote empathy and deeper understanding, I encouraged team members to critique constructively by first stating what they appreciated in each other's ideas before suggesting improvements. This approach aimed to create a supportive environment that fostered creative collaboration.
result: This empathetic approach to leadership helped the team to merge the best aspects of each proposed design, leading to the development of a more efficient and robust gearbox design. The project was not only completed successfully but also strengthened the team's ability to work effectively under stress and complex technical challenges. This experience highlighted the importance of empathy in leadership, particularly in facilitating effective communication and collaboration in engineering projects.
pfr: Initially, leading the gearbox design project felt overwhelming due to the high stakes and technical complexities involved. Each team member brought unique insights and strong opinions on the design process, which, while valuable, sometimes led to tension and indecision. My role as a leader was tested not just on technical grounds but also in harmonizing these diverse viewpoints. I felt a significant responsibility to mediate effectively while ensuring that every team member felt their contributions were valued. This experience was daunting but also immensely enlightening, as it pushed me to develop not just as an engineer but as a leader who must listen and integrate a wide array of perspectives.
learning: From this experience, I learned the crucial role of empathy in leadership, especially in technical projects where diverse expertise and opinions can create friction. Actively encouraging each team member to express and explain their viewpoints led to a richer understanding of the project’s potential and challenges. It highlighted the importance of creating a supportive environment where constructive feedback is encouraged, and every suggestion is considered with respect. Moving forward, I will continue to foster this empathetic leadership style, prioritizing open communication and mutual respect in team settings. This approach not only aids in resolving conflicts but also enhances collective decision-making, leading to more innovative and effective solutions. Additionally, I've learned the importance of structured brainstorming sessions that not only aim to generate ideas but also to build consensus and shared understanding among team members. This project has instilled in me a deeper appreciation for the nuanced role of a leader in engineering projects—balancing technical prowess with interpersonal skills to guide a team towards successful outcomes under constraints. In future projects, I plan to implement structured reflection points throughout the project lifecycle, allowing the team to recalibrate and align more frequently, ensuring smoother progression and heightened collective ownership of the project outcomes.

We ranked the options and discussed their feasibility in detail. * PROTOTYPING AND TESTING: We selected the top three ideas and created low-fidelity prototypes to test their functionality. situation: In our capstone mechanical engineering project, we were tasked with designing an Internet tea maker. The main challenge was to integrate smart technology with traditional tea making, ensuring ease of use, cost-effectiveness, and environmental sustainability. The project required us to not only consider the technical design but also the consumer marketability and operational efficiency.

This involved coordinating with the design, technology, and marketing teams to incorporate their inputs into a cohesive product design. ACTION: To tackle the project, we first conducted a needs analysis to identify key features that potential users valued most, such as temperature control, brewing time settings, and energy efficiency. We held multiple brainstorming sessions to discuss possible features and their implications on cost and manufacturability. During these sessions, we used decision matrix tools to evaluate each feature against criteria such as user demand, technical feasibility, and environmental impact. This helped us prioritize features that offered the best trade-offs between functionality, cost, and sustainability. We also consulted with external experts in smart appliance technology to ensure our design choices were viable and innovative.
result: The final design of our Internet tea maker included optimal features that balanced user needs with practical engineering constraints. We incorporated a customizable brewing temperature control, which was highly requested during our market research, and used environmentally friendly materials to enhance the product’s sustainability. The prototype was well-received during initial testing, with particular praise for its user-friendly interface and energy-efficient operations. From a business perspective, the product was positioned competitively in the smart appliance market, leading to potential interest from manufacturing partners.
pfr: Initially, the task of designing an Internet tea maker was quite overwhelming. The project was complex, involving multiple aspects such as integrating smart technology, ensuring user-friendliness, and maintaining cost-effectiveness. As the team leader, I felt a significant pressure to balance these varied requirements while keeping the project on track. The diverse opinions and suggestions from team members added to the complexity, and at times, it seemed challenging to reach a consensus. However, as we delved deeper into the problem, I found that fostering open communication and systematically evaluating each option allowed us to navigate through the challenges effectively. It was particularly rewarding to see the team come together, appreciate each other’s perspectives, and collaboratively develop a well-rounded product.
learning: Through this experience, I learned the importance of making trade-offs and exercising judgment in engineering projects. Balancing different factors such as functionality, cost, and sustainability is not always straightforward, but by using structured decision-making tools and fostering an inclusive environment, we were able to arrive at a solution that satisfied all major requirements. This project highlighted the necessity of considering multiple perspectives and the value of iterative testing and feedback. Moving forward, I will prioritize thorough needs analysis and stakeholder engagement in my projects. I also realized the importance of continuous learning and consultation with experts to enhance the quality and feasibility of our designs. This experience has reinforced my belief in the importance of structured and empathetic leadership, and I plan to incorporate these approaches in future projects to ensure effective and innovative outcomes.

situation: The advancement of technology in many areas and industries has been rapid. A few of these advancements are around the use of artificial intelligence and others are automation in environments such as warehouses. The implications of this technology advancement are the replacement of jobs particularly those that consist of many repetitive actions/tasks. In warehouse that are being newly built and old warehouses being retrofitted are automated pick-packing solutions. This means that hundreds of employees that worked in this places don't have a job anymore.
task_action: The actions that are to be taken include for those who have lost their job to automation need to find a way that they can gain employment. Another action is using AI ethically so as not to breach privacy and expose children to explicit content as an example. Both these tasks can be challenging however whilst less man power is required in the day to day operations of a warehouse humans still play an important role at some point along the process and it is important that people keep that in mind. Lastly, as engineers it is important to understand how all parties can be affected by technology as it advances. This creates a third task around understanding impacts to businesses, employees and wider society.
result: The technology advances listed here such as warehouse automation, and AI provide many benefits to most parties. However, some parties are certainly negatively affected, this is typically those who have a job which is repetitive and vulnerable to being completed by automation or AI. The benefits of the technology include increased efficiency, and lower consumer prices. The disadvantages are employment, privacy, and security challenges. By automating a warehouse the labour costs of distributing and supplying a product are severely reduced. Due to this the consumers of these products can receive a lower price will the business still maintains the same profit margin. Both automation and AI can significantly improve efficiency in many aspects whether that be professional or admin task around the house. Warehouse automation provides a solution which has a lower risk of error when completing tasks that are repetitive and they can also complete these tasks much faster and for a longer period of time than an employee. This increases efficiency. The disadvantages are the replacement of employees with either automation or AI and this can leave much of the population jobless. It is important to ensure that there is teaching or training that can be provided to these people so that they can find other industries or departments which requires work to be completed. The next challenge is privacy and security. Already, it has become challenging to determine what is factual and what has been created by AI and is incorrect. This is a significant challenge which needs to be addressed. AI is very powerful and has room to become much more powerful and it is important that this is kept in check and AI does not get abused.
pfr: The advances in technology that have been mentioned are exciting and interesting prospects. I find these very interesting to learn about and understand. I can see how they have pros and cons which are listed previously. My understanding of AI at this stage is that humans are still required to train the model. While this can change I believe that there will always be a requirement for human input. Therefore, for me personally I am not afraid of losing my job or career opportunities they will just be different or change. I can however, understand for some how it is very daunting knowing that potentially your skillset can be replaced completely for a cheaper option which means that they can struggle to gain an income. I am always excited to see consumer prices reduced and productivity increased. This applies to both automation and AI. In terms of the other negatives like privacy and security surrounding AI, this is definitely something that I am concerned about. How can an AI model determine right from wrong? What is ethically correct? Should AI show certain images? These are questions that I would like to know about AI. Privacy and security are things in my life that I treasure. By using AI will I lose the ability to these or potentially by not even using them. Another concern around AI content that I have is about showing explicit content. I personally do not. think that AI should be able to output explicit content but I can understand that others would want freedom of speech and information to apply to AI as well. Therefore, whilst I am excited by AI I think it is very important to ensure that it is regulated and always used in a controlled environment and manner.
learning: The learning I have gained from this is that initiatives, programs and regulations should be setup where needed in order to address the negative implications that the advancement in automation and AI has. Some suggestions for this are training sessions to provide skills to workers that lose jobs to this technology, programs to help these people find other industries that require workers. And regulations around the use of AI in a sense that it should be used productively and explicit content should be regulated. A way to limit how much personal data and information AI has access to could be a good idea as well.

Customer focus: I provided a solution (change or refund) as soon as possible and apologized to the customer for the wrong order.
result: This lead into reduced errors from our side meaning orders were delivered with accuracy, and this resulted in higher customer satisfaction rate. I also arranged for two senior members to mentor the less experienced team members, providing them with guidance on using the necessary tools and algorithms like YOLOv8, CNNs, and LSTMs. Furthermore, I maintained an open line of communication with our faculty advisor to seek advice and ensure that the project aligned with academic standards and expectations.

My role as a team leader helped me develop strong leadership and project management skills, which were acknowledged by both my peers and professors.

situation: I was working as at Spruson and Ferguson with my client on the patent for a new medical imaging algorithm that would revolutionise the medical industry. Unfortunately, a competitor had also developed a similar software soon after we published ours, raising concerns that they may have potentially infringed on our patent.
task_action: My task was to make protect my clients patent by making sure that the competitor’s software did not infringe any intellectual property or patent laws. Action: I did this by conducting a thorough patent review and analysis. I went through a comprehensive review of what our patent covered, then I used the knowledge I had from being a 3rd year engineering student to understand what parts of our software was covered by our patents. I then analysed our competitor’s software and found what parts of it infringed on our patents. I then consulted other patent attorneys at my law firm to figure out whether we had a potential case, which we did. I then filed a cease-and-desist letter to our competitor, telling them the specific parts of their software which infringed our patents. We then prepared for a potential lawsuit.
result: We were prepared for a lawsuit but fortunately the competitor backed down. We also found other areas that could be patented which allowed us to better protect our medical imaging software. The removal of our competitor’s software gave my company the edge in the medical imaging market, allowing us to gain a solid lead over our competitors. We will continue looking for other potential breaches but there have been few since.
pfr: I found the experience of handling patents for this company to be very fulfilling and rewarding. I was continuously challenged and have managed to experience a multitude of different perspectives when it comes to medical imaging. It is vital to protect our intellectual properties from potential infringement from competitors. It helped me develop strategic thinking, thorough analysis and an assertive legal mindset. Initially I felt out of my league. I am only a third-year engineer. However, I was determined to help my client defend himself against this patent infringement and ensure that their hard work hasn't been undermined. As the case went on, my confidence grew, and the enjoyment I gained grew with it. The work was challenging and highly stimulating. I felt very satisfied after completing the case.
learning: My meticulous approach to patents did work well, but I now realise that I should have been more prepared. If I was more meticulous with protect all aspects of the patent, this would have been a clear win rather than a close call. In the future I will endeavour to be more proactive in filing for patents rather than being reactive. This experience proved the importance of patents in our system. It is obvious that the key to keeping a competitive edge is by having a proactive IP strategy which allows for the protection of our new innovations and continuous market dominance. This experience also highlighted how important IP awareness is, especially for stakeholders. Moving forward I will be more proactive with finding and defending my client’s patents, look to learn more from other disciplines that could fall under my patents, and educate any stakeholders about the dangers of not protecting their IP. By doing this, I will strengthen my client’s IP protection which will keep their competitive edge and reduce the risk of future problems due to IP disputes. This will allow my clients to focus more on their innovative spirit and furthering the future of technology.

This document also served as a log for any decisions made during our meetings.
result: By implementing this structured approach, we were able to resolve our conflicts and agree on a unified strategy for completing the project. The team members who were initially absent became more involved after understanding the critical situation and seeing a clear plan in place. We successfully completed the project on time, receiving positive feedback from our professor for our collaboration and problem-solving skills. topic: Initiative and the willingness to make decisions in the face of uncertainty
situation: In our Advanced Mechanical Design course, our team was assigned the task of developing a cost-effective and efficient gearbox for the crane prototype. As the project progressed, we encountered a significant challenge when our initial gearbox design did not meet the performance criteria during testing, and the deadline for the final submission was only a few weeks away.
task_action: As the team leader, I was responsible for steering the project back on track. The critical task was to quickly come up with an alternative design that met the performance requirements without exceeding our limited budget and remaining timeline. The uncertainty regarding the availability of materials and the feasibility of new design modifications added to the complexity of the task. ACTION: I initiated an emergency team meeting to discuss our options and brainstorm new ideas. Recognizing the urgency of the situation, I encouraged a proactive and creative approach from all team members. We utilized a combination of round-robin and gallery methods in our brainstorming sessions to ensure every idea was heard and considered. After generating several alternative designs, we evaluated each based on criteria such as cost, manufacturability, and performance efficiency. We selected the most promising design and quickly prototyped it to validate its feasibility.
result: The redesigned gearbox not only met the required performance criteria but also proved to be more cost-effective, reducing the overall production cost by 25%. The team successfully met the project deadline, and our gearbox design was commended during the course review for its innovation and practical applicability. This experience significantly enhanced my ability to lead under pressure, make decisive choices in uncertain conditions, and foster a collaborative team environment. It underscored the importance of adaptability and rapid problem-solving in engineering, skills that are critical to my future career development.

Knowing that the success of the project hinged on our ability to quickly pivot and innovate under constraints was daunting. The initial failure of our design was a significant setback, and the weight of expectation to deliver a viable solution was immense. Throughout this process, I was both nervous about our ability to meet the deadline and motivated by the determination of my team. Leading the team through this uncertainty, I found myself constantly balancing optimism with the practicality of our design choices, which was mentally taxing yet incredibly enlightening.
learning: The experience taught me several valuable lessons about engineering, teamwork, and leadership. Firstly, the importance of flexibility in problem-solving became clear. Being able to adapt and consider alternative solutions quickly is crucial, especially when initial plans falter. I learned that effective leadership in the face of uncertainty involves not just directing efforts but also fostering an environment where every team member feels empowered to contribute creatively. This collective approach not only enriched our brainstorming sessions but also expedited our decision-making process, allowing us to develop a more efficient and cost-effective gearbox design. Furthermore, I gained insight into the psychological aspects of leading a team through challenges. Maintaining team morale and confidence, especially when the outcome is uncertain, is as important as the technical decisions being made. In future projects, I will focus more on this aspect of team dynamics, ensuring that I provide both clear direction and emotional support to my team members. This experience also underscored the importance of robust, structured decision-making processes in engineering design. Going forward, I will implement a more systematic approach to design challenges, incorporating regular review checkpoints and contingency planning from the outset. This will help mitigate risks and ensure that the team remains on track, even when unexpected issues arise. In conclusion, this project not only enhanced my technical and leadership skills but also deepened my understanding of the human elements in engineering projects. I am now more aware of my capabilities and limitations as a leader and am better prepared to handle similar situations in the future, ensuring both project success and team well-being.

topic: The design process phasing and approaches
situation: Our group needed to design a tea maker that was based on an IoT system and I was given the task of designing a subsystem of a loose-leaf tea dispenser. It was stated that the customer needs storage for four different types of tea in the machine and tea should be dispensed automatically.
task_action: When the tasks were equally divided within the team, I started to plan for my part. We needed to communicate our progress and design with our team so that it wouldn't mismatch the whole machine at the end. I used the design process phase (NEEDS--->CONCEPTUAL DESIGN--->PRELIMINARY DESIGN--->DETAIL DESIGN) graph as my reference to track my progress. Initially, I reviewed the customer's requirements to inform my design approach. I organized my workload over six weeks: dedicating the first three weeks to the conceptual design, the next two weeks to the preliminary design phase, and the final week to the detailed design. Our team analyzed the NEEDS of the customers and made a list of features(sub-systems) that can be included in the machine. We distributed the sub-systems to each person on the team to ease the process of building the machine. In the CONCEPTUAL DESIGN phase, I generated multiple conceptual designs based on the requirements. I conducted extensive research on various dispensing systems analogous to our project, which involved dispensing tea leaves. Through a week of brainstorming and reviewing different mechanisms, I expedited this phase to two weeks by maintaining regular communication with my team. I illustrated six conceptual ideas on paper and presented them for team discussion. After a detailed review, we refined and eliminated infeasible ideas, ultimately narrowing down to three preliminary designs. During the PRELIMINARY DESIGN phase, which spanned two weeks, we focused on material selection and refining our chosen design. We established key parameters such as cost, reliability, and sustainability. The designs were ranked based on these criteria, and the top-ranked design was selected for further development. Additionally, I developed the Technical Performance Measures (TPMs) and the House of Quality for this sub-system. In the DETAILED DESIGN phase, I translated the selected preliminary ideas into a CAD model and constructed a small prototype to verify that the actual test parameters aligned with our assumptions. Finally, I completed the final design, which the team agreed would seamlessly integrate into our tea dispensing machine.
result: As a result, I completed my task beforehand with much more efficiency and meeting the requirements of the client. The efficiency was primarily achieved by dividing the machine into sub-systems and allowing me to work on one sub-system while maintaining ongoing communication about their progress within the team. My design was reliable within the parameters and was meeting the client's requirements. This caused the seamless integration of my sub-system to integrate perfectly into our final machine design. Finally, the use of the design process phase graph allowed me to effectively track my progress. This facilitated the timely completion of each phase, ensuring that the project stayed on schedule.
pfr: Initially, when we were given a task to design a tea maker, our team was not organized properly and had no organized flow in making the system. I proposed the plan of dividing the machine into sub-parts and equally dividing it according to their majors or strengths. This was done to control the flow of the process and to be organized rather than having it all in one plate. I also proposed to have a flow chart for the design process and to follow that flow chart for designing the sub-system. My main reason for this was to collaborate effectively as a team while allowing individual creativity to flourish. This structured yet flexible methodology significantly improved my workflow and the quality of our team's final design. Furthermore, this fostered a sense of ownership and responsibility for me, as I had a clear role and could see how my contributions fit into the larger picture. I did have some designs that were a conflict of interest within the team but debating about that and improving the design from constructive feedback helped me to get the final design.
learning: From this experience, I learned about leadership, teamwork, the importance of communication, the Importance of Organization, ownership and responsibility, and Collaborative Problem-Solving for designing a system. I worked as a team member yet a flexible approach allowed me to integrate my diverse perspectives and skills towards the final design. Proposing and implementing a flow chart and structured plan required me to take on a leadership role. This experience improved my ability to guide a team, delegate tasks, and manage a project effectively. Despite the initial lack of organization, adapting to a new plan and being open to different ideas taught me the importance of flexibility in project management. Being able to adjust and refine our approach was key to our success. I learned that having a clear structure and organized plan is crucial for the success of any project. Dividing the machine into sub-parts and assigning tasks based on individual strengths helped streamline our process and avoid confusion. The conflicts we encountered highlighted the importance of open and respectful communication. Constructive debates and idea sharing were essential in identifying the best solutions for the overall design.
